layers.title: Who is bound?
layers.summary: Identify the legal entity, jurisdiction and applicable domestic implementation before assigning a bank requirement.
layers.question: Which rule applies to this entity, account and date?
layers.boundary: Basel standards are not themselves supranational law.

layers.title: Bank buffers & stable funding
layers.summary: LCR examines a 30-day stress horizon; NSFR examines stable funding over a one-year horizon.
layers.question: Which assets and funding qualify, and what is transferable?
layers.boundary: Neither ratio establishes capacity to execute a particular intraday payment.

layers.title: Payment timing & credit
layers.summary: Track opening resources, incoming flows, deadlines and the largest cumulative shortfall.
layers.question: Who supplies the interval when incoming money is late?
layers.boundary: Daily totals conceal peak funding needs; public data gaps do not prove missing internal monitoring.

layers.title: Prefunding, netting & withdrawal
layers.summary: System rules determine release, position limits, queues and whether funding can leave.
layers.question: Can this balance fund another payment here—and can it be withdrawn elsewhere?
layers.boundary: CHIPS reuse does not confer unrestricted outward withdrawal. SWIFT does not inherit CHIPS rules.

layers.title: Turn assets into funding
layers.summary: Separate asset market value, accepted collateral value and remaining credit capacity.
layers.question: Is the asset eligible, pledged correctly and fundable before the deadline?
layers.boundary: A tokenized fund share does not automatically inherit the collateral treatment of its underlying securities.

layers.title: Holder rights & exit
layers.summary: Redemption depends on the holder, issuer, jurisdiction, procedure and payout route.
layers.question: Who can redeem, into what, how much and when?
layers.boundary: Token transfer, issuer processing and bank availability are separate events.

layers.title: Quotes & available inventory
layers.summary: A route needs a willing counterparty or available exit inventory at the requested size and price.
layers.question: Who replenishes the liquidity after a one-way flow?
layers.boundary: 24/7 access and atomic execution do not guarantee price or unlimited capacity.

layers.title: Failure & replenishment
layers.summary: Test late receipts, collateral markdowns, unavailable funding and counterparty failure.
layers.question: Who still owes payment, and what can be delayed or released?
layers.boundary: A successful pilot is not proof of stressed capacity or loss allocation.

legal_process_hub.title: Legal process
legal_process_hub.subtitle: Follow a transaction from a claimed right to a posted, repairable result.

steps.title: Name the claim
steps.question: What right is being created, transferred, pledged, redeemed, or paid?
steps.explanation: Start with the instrument and obligation. A share, entitlement, bank deposit, token, collateral interest, and payment instruction carry different rights and obligors.
steps.actors: Issuer or obligor; holder; intermediary.
steps.required_evidence: Instrument terms; named obligor; holder-rights description; governing-law clause.
steps.output: A statement of who owes what to whom under which terms.
steps.boundary: Technical possession or a token transfer is not a complete description of legal ownership or discharge.

steps.title: Draw the actor perimeter
steps.question: Which legal entity performs each function?
steps.explanation: Separate parent, regulated subsidiary, depository, clearing agency, bank, transfer agent, wallet provider, network, and vendor. One organization can wear several hats; each has separate duties.
steps.actors: Legal operator; regulated subsidiary; service provider; supervisor.
steps.required_evidence: Entity chart; registration or charter; service agreement; supervisory route.
steps.output: A role map for issuer, recordkeeper, operator, cash obligor, risk manager, and remedy authority.
steps.boundary: A shared brand, partnership, or technology stack does not merge legal entities or permissions.

steps.title: Establish permission
steps.question: What allows this entity to perform this function now?
steps.explanation: Match the activity to a live authority: terms, registration, operating circular, rulebook, designation, order, exemption, or no-action position. Keep scope and effective date attached.
steps.actors: Regulator; registered intermediary; operator; participant.
steps.required_evidence: Statute or regulation; registration/order/letter; effective rulebook; scope and expiry terms.
steps.output: A permission statement with its date, product, participant, and volume limits.
steps.boundary: A proposal, pilot, announcement, or generic FMI label grants no unlisted permission.

steps.title: Identify the authoritative record
steps.question: If books disagree, which record decides the holder, balance, or obligation?
steps.explanation: Issuer registers, transfer-agent files, depository entitlement books, bank accounts, and networks can each describe a different legal relationship. Identify the controlling record for this issue and event.
steps.actors: Issuer; recordkeeping transfer agent; depository; bank; network operator.
steps.required_evidence: Recordkeeping agreement; record clause; reconciliation design; correction rights.
steps.output: A record hierarchy and named reconciliation point.
steps.boundary: A distributed ledger can be linked to a master file without becoming the legal register for every asset on it.

steps.title: Bind the instruction
steps.question: Who may send, validate, and delegate an instruction?
steps.explanation: A valid instruction has an authorized sender, authentication, eligibility checks, and rules for rejection, cancellation, queueing, and delegation.
steps.actors: Customer or participant; bank or broker; operator; technology provider.
steps.required_evidence: Access agreement; authentication rules; instruction lifecycle; vendor-control terms.
steps.output: A trace from mandate to accepted instruction, including who can stop it before execution.
steps.boundary: A transmitted message, signed wallet action, or broadcast transaction is not necessarily accepted or irrevocable.

steps.title: Clear the obligation and assemble resources
steps.question: Who matches, nets, collateralizes, funds, or guarantees it?
steps.explanation: Some routes pass instructions onward; others create CCP obligations, prefunded positions, or bank-credit exposure. Map margin, collateral, liquidity, netting, and default resources.
steps.actors: CCP; clearing member; settlement bank; liquidity provider; collateral manager.
steps.required_evidence: Clearing rules; margin/liquidity rules; funding-account terms; default waterfall.
steps.output: A resources map of gross and net obligation, pledged resources, funding source, and residual exposure.
steps.boundary: Fast execution or a smaller net payment does not prove liquidity, collateral, or default exposure disappeared.

steps.title: Settle each leg and name finality
steps.question: What asset moves, in which accounts, and when is each obligation final?
steps.explanation: Securities delivery, cash posting, token transfer, payout, and redemption can have different finality points. Name whether the event is technical confirmation, book-entry posting, contractual discharge, or statutory finality.
steps.actors: Settlement operator; depository; bank; cash issuer; participant.
steps.required_evidence: Settlement rule; cash-asset identity; account-entry timing; finality and insolvency clause.
steps.output: A two-leg settlement receipt with named assets, timestamps, and finality rules.
steps.boundary: A confirmed ledger event does not prove the other leg, legal discharge, redemption, or bank availability.

steps.title: Post, reconcile and service
steps.question: Which books update, and who administers rights after settlement?
steps.explanation: Completion creates customer, participant, depository, transfer-agent, issuer, and sometimes network postings. Servicing covers distributions, votes, corporate actions, maturity, redemption, and reporting.
steps.actors: Recordkeeper; custodian; issuer; administrator; participant.
steps.required_evidence: Posting records; reconciliation schedule; servicing agreement; exception reports.
steps.output: A reconciled record chain and named administrator for ongoing holder rights.
steps.boundary: A transaction receipt does not prove all books reconciled or later servicing occurred.

steps.title: Repair, allocate loss and prove the result
steps.question: Who can correct an error, what happens on default or outage, and what proves performance?
steps.explanation: A durable process names correction powers, reversals, disputes, collateral realization, loss allocation, recovery, and wind-down. Separate written controls from observed stress.
steps.actors: Operator; supervisor; default manager; service provider; affected holder.
steps.required_evidence: Correction rule; default/recovery plan; loss-allocation rule; incident or stress record.
steps.output: A remedy map naming actor, loss bearer, and evidence level.
steps.boundary: Immutability or a service promise does not remove insolvency, correction, or loss-allocation questions.

layers.title: Legal claim and governing law
layers.summary: The instrument, obligor, holder right, and governing law define the right before any technology moves it.
layers.question: What legal right exists and what law governs it?
layers.boundary: A network event does not replace the underlying contract or property rule.

layers.title: Permission and supervision
layers.summary: Registration, designation, charter, and service eligibility route authority to a specific entity and function.
layers.question: Who authorizes and supervises this function?
layers.boundary: FMI terminology alone does not create account access or jurisdiction.

layers.title: FMI standards and domestic implementation
layers.summary: PFMI provides the international framework. U.S. implementation separates Title VIII designation, Board risk standards under Regulation HH, SEC clearing-agency rules and the Fed’s policy for its own systems.
layers.question: Which rule actually applies to this legal operator and function?
layers.boundary: HH risk-standard scope excludes SEC-registered clearing agencies and CFTC-registered DCOs. Transfer-agency functions alone do not automatically establish FMU status.

layers.title: Operating constitution
layers.summary: Rulebooks and participant agreements assign duties, control instructions, and set processing rules.
layers.question: What operating rules bind the participants?
layers.boundary: A public product description is not the executed operating constitution.

layers.title: Authoritative records and accounts
layers.summary: Each legal relationship has a controlling book and a reconciliation path.
layers.question: Which records control each relationship?
layers.boundary: Several records can be authoritative for different questions; they need not compete for one universal truth.

layers.title: Risk, finality and remedy
layers.summary: Margin, liquidity, finality, recovery, and loss allocation determine what happens when routine processing fails.
layers.question: How are resources protected, settlement finalized, and failures repaired?
layers.boundary: A normal-day result does not prove stress capacity or recovery performance.

cases.title: Linked electronic securities records
cases.status: Proposed SEC architecture; not operative law at saved cutoff.
cases.summary: The SEC proposal would accommodate linked electronic systems, including a blockchain or DLT component, while one registered recordkeeping transfer agent retains responsibility and exclusive control of the master securityholder file.
cases.boundary: It would not authorize every chain, bridge, wallet, or vendor as a transfer agent, clearing agency, or FMI.

steps.finding: A security issue and holder right remain the starting legal object.
steps.gap: Specific issue terms are not supplied by the proposal.

steps.finding: One registered recordkeeping transfer agent would remain accountable.
steps.gap: Each linked-system vendor contract needs review.

steps.finding: Release 34-106246/S7-2026-30 was proposed.
steps.gap: No final rule or compliance date at cutoff.

steps.finding: A master file could span linked systems while the transfer agent retains exclusive control.
steps.gap: Actual reconciliation is issue-specific.

steps.finding: Transfer-agent controls would govern record updates.
steps.gap: No universal wallet or chain instruction rule.

steps.finding: The proposal itself supplies no clearing or funding arrangement.
steps.gap: Identify the resources required by the actual transaction.

steps.finding: A chain event could form part of recordkeeping.
steps.gap: It would not itself establish DvP or legal title finality for every issue.

steps.finding: The accountable transfer agent would maintain the master file.
steps.gap: Servicing terms remain issue-specific.

steps.finding: Named legal responsibility would remain with the transfer agent.
steps.gap: Existing duties, proposed changes and actual provider remedies require separate review.

cases.title: SEC crypto-asset classification and investment-contract FAQs
cases.status: Corporation Finance staff guidance issued September 25, 2026; nonbinding and not Commission action.
cases.summary: Nine staff answers apply the March Commission interpretation to two functionality clocks, staking receipts, pure-receipt ownership and no-rehypothecation conditions, utility marketing, successor promises, post-functional development, central-party absence, buybacks and secondary-platform promoter status.
cases.boundary: The FAQs refine legal analysis but create no rule, registration, exemption, safe harbor, venue permission, asset approval or operating receipt. The March interpretation remains the Commission-level object, and Regulation Crypto Assets remains proposed.

steps.finding: Asset classification uses the Commission's definitions of functional and decentralized, while fulfillment of essential-managerial-effort promises uses the functionality or decentralization threshold the issuer itself represented.
steps.gap: An exact asset still needs current system facts, rights and value-source evidence; satisfying an issuer-authored milestone does not itself establish the Commission's classification test.

steps.finding: The relevant actors include the issuer, affiliates, agents, any Rule 405 promoter, a successor assuming promises, a receipt issuer or custodian and a protocol-based liquid-staking provider.
steps.gap: A brand, developer, platform or successor label does not establish the exact legal relationship or promoter status.

steps.finding: The FAQs are issued staff guidance applying Release 33-11412/34-105020 and cite the Commission view in the proposed Regulation Crypto Assets release.
steps.gap: They do not amend the interpretation, make Rule 400 or Form TR operative, approve an offering or grant any intermediary permission.

steps.finding: A pure receipt evidences the depositor's continuing ownership of a stated deposited asset without changing its rights or adding separate economics.
steps.gap: Verify deposit and ownership records, exact token terms, reward source, liens and whether the issuer can transfer, lend, pledge, rehypothecate or otherwise use the asset.

steps.finding: Marketing current utility and indefinite non-profit-focused aspirations likely do not, without more, promise essential managerial efforts; listing alone does not make a platform a promoter absent Rule 405.
steps.gap: Review the full communication channel, authorization, specificity, profit framing and platform relationship rather than relying on labels.

steps.finding: A qualifying receipt leaves the issuer unable to use or expose the deposited asset to third-party claims; post-functional buyback announcements are not managerial promises merely because they alter supply.
steps.gap: Custody, balance-sheet use, insolvency exposure, funding source, pool economics and any pre-functional yield or return framing remain transaction-specific.

steps.finding: The FAQs classify relationships and promises; they do not identify settlement assets, discharge rules, finality or failed-leg treatment.
steps.gap: Every securities, crypto, receipt and cash leg still requires its own account, custody, finality and insolvency analysis.

steps.finding: Once a system is functional, securing, maintaining, improving or enhancing it and facilitating network effects do not involve essential managerial efforts under the cited Commission view.
steps.gap: Separate ordinary post-functional service from unfulfilled issuer promises, new profit-linked undertakings and the actual administration of holder rights.

steps.finding: Successor assumption preserves the promise relationship; by contrast, issuer statements likely do not create a new investment contract once a functional system has no central party capable of controlling success or failure.
steps.gap: Prove the succession instrument, remaining obligations, control distribution, abandonment or completion facts and any later promise rather than treating a handoff or decentralization slogan as dispositive.

cases.title: SEC adviser and regulated-fund crypto custody proposal
cases.status: Commission proposal issued October 1, 2026; not final, effective, compliant or operating.
cases.summary: The 760-page proposal would create asset-specific adviser self-custody only while no qualified custodian will maintain the covered asset, add a conditional State trust company route, apply fund-board oversight, treat key possession as custody, require segregation, joint authorization, cybersecurity, independent control reporting and Article 8 treatment, and permit qualifying onchain regulatory records with examiner-readable offchain completion.
cases.boundary: The proposal grants no present permission, does not cover every crypto asset or account, supplies no general exchange-custody or DeFi exception, does not make a chain the universal ownership record and does not prove a named adviser, fund, custodian, asset, wallet, protocol or transaction complies or operates.

steps.finding: Custody scope depends on the crypto asset's legal classification and account type; self-custody would also require a written Article 8 financial-asset and securities-intermediary election.
steps.gap: Determine the exact asset, account, client right, obligor, governing law and whether the mandatory entitlement frame matches the intended holding relationship.

steps.finding: Adviser, designated supervised key holders, regulated-fund board, independent accountant, qualified custodian, State trust company, technology provider, client and regulator retain distinct functions.
steps.gap: Prove each legal entity, related-person status, delegation, vendor access, board role and contract rather than using a shared brand or wallet label.

steps.finding: Proposed rules 223-1(b)(7), 17f-8 and 17f-9 would create residual self-custody and conditional State trust company routes; self-custody would require a written no-qualified-custodian determination re-tested at least quarterly.
steps.gap: Federal Register publication, final action, effective and compliance dates, asset eligibility, exact custodian availability and route-specific compliance remain unproved.

steps.finding: Required crypto records could be maintained onchain only when true, accurate, current, retained, promptly produced in human-readable form and supplemented offchain for ownership, identity or other missing information.
steps.gap: Name the authoritative record for ownership, customer positions, accounting, statements, correction and disputes; a public address or explorer is not automatically complete.

steps.finding: Possession of any portion of key materials can establish custody; only designated supervised persons may hold keys and at least two people, including management, must jointly authorize movement.
steps.gap: Inspect the actual MPC or multisignature design, recovery shares, limits, client access, vendor access, authentication and accepted-instruction lifecycle.

steps.finding: Per-client address segregation, State trust financial statements, internal control reports, network reconciliation and related-cash limits would create a custody protection layer.
steps.gap: Capital, insurance, collateral, liquidity, indemnity, rehypothecation, platform prefunding and default resources remain arrangement-specific or open for comment.

steps.finding: The proposal recognizes network records and custody controls but does not propose a general exception for assets held on non-custodian trading platforms and does not create a universal DeFi route.
steps.gap: Prove venue authority, cash leg, delivery-versus-payment, technical confirmation, legal discharge, staking or protocol control and finality for each leg.

steps.finding: Addresses, balances, transactions, client statements or electronic views, Article 8 agreements, annual reviews, board records and independent reports would form a joined but multi-record custody constitution.
steps.gap: Corporate actions, airdrops, staking, privacy data, accounting entries, tax, long-term access and reconciliation exceptions still require exact operating evidence.

steps.finding: The proposal would require cyber response and recovery, board notice for serious events, control-report exceptions, transition to a newly available custodian and an Article 8 creditor-priority frame.
steps.gap: Actual reversibility, insurance payment, insolvency priority, protocol loss, key compromise, custodian failure, client compensation and Commission loss reporting remain unproved or unresolved.

cases.title: CLARITY Act EHF26724 proposed market structure
cases.status: Sponsors' final draft released September 14, 2026; not filed substitute text or operative law.
cases.summary: The 635-page draft retains four divisions and would create coordinated SEC, Treasury, banking-agency and CFTC routes for digital assets, spot intermediaries and controlled DeFi. It adds affiliate-conflict and proprietary-trading controls, a stablecoin deposit-flight circuit breaker, credit-union parity, revised developer protections and a permanent digital-asset ethics regime.
cases.boundary: This case changes future qualification questions only. It grants no present permission, classification, registration or compliance status to any Hub actor, asset, protocol or transaction.

steps.finding: Network-token and ancillary-asset provisions would create new federal classification and disclosure branches for some digital-asset transactions.
steps.gap: Enactment, implementing rules and product-specific facts remain necessary; the draft does not classify every existing Hub asset.

steps.finding: The draft separates SEC/Treasury, banking-agency and CFTC functions and adds activity-based controlled-DeFi tests plus explicit vertically integrated affiliate controls.
steps.gap: Each named legal entity, affiliate link and control fact must still be proved; a brand or protocol label is not the regulated person.

steps.finding: Spot exchanges, brokers, dealers, custodians and persons controlling covered DeFi functions would receive proposed registration or compliance routes after the required rules.
steps.gap: EHF26724 is not law, its amendment fields remain blank, and no Hub actor receives a current registration, exemption or charter power from it.

steps.finding: Customer-property, segregation, custody, disclosure and books-and-records provisions would add qualification requirements by intermediary function.
steps.gap: The draft does not make a blockchain the authoritative legal record for every asset or replace issue-specific contracts and record hierarchies.

steps.finding: Revised developer protections would expressly cover specified non-controlling development, validation, node, oracle, bandwidth and user-controlled wallet activities for named money-transmission categories.
steps.gap: The shield is proposed and function-specific, removes the earlier express 18 U.S.C. 1960 reference, and does not create a derivatives or general-conduct immunity.

steps.finding: Stablecoin rewards would carry a contingent Treasury deposit-flight circuit breaker, while federal and insured credit unions would gain express parity for otherwise-authorized DLT and digital-asset activity.
steps.gap: No deposit flight has been determined, no circuit-breaker rule exists, and asset, liquidity, reserve, credit and balance-sheet exposure remain arrangement-specific.

steps.finding: The proposal regulates intermediary and customer-protection functions without declaring technical confirmation a universal legal-finality event.
steps.gap: Payment, securities, digital-commodity, custody and insolvency rules still determine finality for each leg and legal relationship.

steps.finding: Registration, customer-property, disclosure and reporting provisions would add function-specific recordkeeping and servicing duties.
steps.gap: Issuer, transfer-agent, custodian, exchange, broker, bank and network records remain separate and would require implementing rules and contracts.

steps.finding: The draft adds affiliate-conflict controls, exchange proprietary-trading limits, preserved state consumer-protection routes and a permanent ethics enforcement regime with specified federal and state remedies.
steps.gap: These are proposed duties, not present findings that a named Hub company or official complied, violated, caused harm or bears a particular loss.

cases.title: Tokenized NMS Stock Innovation Exemption
cases.status: Effective SEC exemptive order through September 17, 2031; no operating TSV established at the saved cutoff.
cases.summary: Release 34-106402 conditionally exempts a Tokenized Securities Venue from the Exchange Act definition of exchange and a qualifying own-account AMM liquidity provider from the dealer definition. Permissioned pools must use auditable public applications deployed on public, permissionless DLT; at least one leg must be Tokenized NMS Stock, and the other may be another such stock, any non-security crypto asset or a tokenized money market fund.
cases.boundary: The order opens a venue category, not a named venue, chain, token or product. A complete TSV notice must run for at least 30 calendar days, and issuer, issuance, record, custody, clearing, settlement, participant and failure rules remain separate.

steps.finding: The pool must contain Tokenized NMS Stock carrying the same company interest, voting, dividend and residual rights as the underlying NMS stock.
steps.gap: An actual issue, tokenizer, holder-rights instrument and Securities Act route must still be identified. Synthetic exposures, rights and warrants are outside the defined stock category.

steps.finding: The order separates the TSV operator, affiliates, tokenizers, liquidity providers, participants, registered activities and service providers and requires public conflict disclosure.
steps.gap: No Hub company or ecosystem is named as a TSV, Covered Firm, tokenizer, participant or service provider. Each legal entity and role must be proved from the eventual notice and contracts.

steps.finding: The Commission order is effective and supplies two temporary conditional exemptions through September 17, 2031.
steps.gap: No venue may operate until its complete public notice has run for at least 30 calendar days. Existing broker-dealer and other participant obligations are not broadly waived.

steps.finding: Token holders must receive equivalent stock rights and the TSV must disclose the tokenization, legal and technical evaluation, wallets, chain, contracts, keys and correction-related controls.
steps.gap: The order does not make the AMM, wallet or chain the issuer's authoritative ownership record or grant transfer-agent relief. The actual record hierarchy remains issue-specific.

steps.finding: Participant access is permissioned even though the application must be public and deployed on public, permissionless DLT. The TSV sets admission standards, pool parameters and administrative controls.
steps.gap: The first notice must identify identity checks, differentiated treatment, upgrade, pause, override, privacy, MEV and service-provider controls. Public infrastructure does not mean public market access.

steps.finding: A Covered Firm may provide own-account Tokenized NMS Stock liquidity and disclose agreements, fees, rebates and token incentives. The TSV itself may not finance purchases or lend, borrow or hypothecate assets on the venue.
steps.gap: The order supplies no CCP, custody, external financing, haircut, default waterfall or token-inventory receipt. Persistent net XRP or other token inventory remains unproved.

steps.finding: The order permits a venue architecture capable of self-custody, extended hours and faster settlement and requires disclosure of actual clearing and settlement arrangements.
steps.gap: Near-instant settlement is a possible benefit, not a required or proven legal-finality result. Each securities, crypto, money-market-fund and cash leg needs its own finality and insolvency analysis.

steps.finding: The TSV must retain detailed interest, execution, permissioning, wallet, fee, halt, ADV, notice and event records; equivalent voting, dividend and issuer-communication rights must continue.
steps.gap: Trade reporting within ten minutes is not the same as SIP reporting or proof that issuer, transfer-agent, custodian and participant books reconciled. Corporate-action servicing remains product-specific.

steps.finding: Underlying-market halts must carry across; significant operational events require participant and SEC notice and remediation; records remain examinable by the Commission.
steps.gap: The order can require disclosure that surveillance, complaint or other protections are absent. It does not itself provide a complete customer-loss, clearing-default, custody-failure or smart-contract remedy.

steps.finding: Posting joins securities and corresponding cash entries.
steps.gap: Trace holder-level servicing through the issuer and participant arrangements.

steps.finding: Service rules allocate operating responsibilities.

innovation_exemption_overlay.title: Which tracked technologies overlap the Innovation Exemption?
innovation_exemption_overlay.subtitle: Twenty governed ecosystems compared against the order's venue, chain, asset, record, liquidity and settlement conditions.
innovation_exemption_overlay.summary: The order creates a permission category, not a vendor list. This matrix identifies where a tracked system has a technically or institutionally relevant component and what must still be proved before it can be called part of a Tokenized Securities Venue.
innovation_exemption_overlay.boundary: Every row remains not selected and not operating under Release 34-106402. Core candidate means architectural overlap only; it does not establish legal qualification, integration, issuer acceptance, a TSV notice, an eligible pool or observed trading.

status_legend.label: Core technical candidate
status_legend.meaning: A public-chain execution or AMM layer appears capable of addressing the order's core technical surface, subject to the exact deployment and every legal condition.

status_legend.label: Conditional or unresolved candidate
status_legend.meaning: A relevant component exists, but the public-permissionless, AMM, rights or exact deployment fit is unresolved or depends on a specific network variant.

status_legend.label: Supporting control layer
status_legend.meaning: The system could support issuance, recordkeeping, identity, custody, data, interoperability, liquidity, cash or settlement without itself being the qualifying TSV base venue.

status_legend.label: Outside the core venue design
status_legend.meaning: The tracked system as currently described is permissioned, proprietary or functionally different from the required public-permissionless AMM venue, though it may connect externally.

gates.title: Venue and clock
gates.rule: A U.S.-person TSV must publish the complete required notice at least 30 calendar days before operating and notify the SEC within one business day.
gates.watch: First notice, operator, affiliates, operating date and later material amendments.

gates.title: Public-chain application
gates.rule: The smart contracts and DLT applications must be auditable, public and deployed on public, permissionless DLT while market access remains permissioned.
gates.watch: Named chain, contract addresses, code, upgrades, pause or override keys and admission controls.

gates.title: Stock and issuer rights
gates.rule: At least one pool leg must be Tokenized NMS Stock with equivalent economic and governance rights; unaffiliated third-party tokenization carries a separate issuer notice and objection clock.
gates.watch: Named stock, sponsor or tokenizer, issuer receipt or objection, rights audit and transfer-agent record model.

gates.title: Permitted pair asset
gates.rule: The other leg may be another Tokenized NMS Stock, any non-security crypto asset or a tokenized money market fund.
gates.watch: Named pair, asset classification, issuer or fund, redemption chain, market depth and route share.

gates.title: AMM and liquidity provider
gates.rule: A Covered Firm may provide own-account Tokenized NMS Stock liquidity under the dealer exemption; agreements, compensation and token incentives must be disclosed.
gates.watch: Pool curves, liquidity provider, gross and net inventory, financing, hedges, fees, rebates and incentives.

gates.title: Caps, data and halts
gates.rule: Symbol and ADV caps, ten-minute machine-readable transaction reporting and underlying-market halt synchronization constrain the lane.
gates.watch: Eligible tier, volume utilization, transaction feed, after-hours pricing, issuer events and pause history.

gates.title: Separate regulated functions
gates.rule: The order does not supply issuance, transfer-agent, custody, clearing-agency, Investment Company Act, bank-money or participant-wide relief.
gates.watch: Exact legal entities, registrations, service agreements, books, customer-property treatment and affiliate separation.

gates.title: Settlement and remedy
gates.rule: Clearing and settlement arrangements, cybersecurity, BCDR, corporate actions and material operational events must be disclosed, but the order does not itself create finality or a complete loss waterfall.
gates.watch: Two-leg settlement receipt, authoritative record, cash discharge, correction powers, default rules and observed incidents.

overlaps.overlap: XRPL is a public execution network with native exchange and AMM functions; XRP could fit the non-security-crypto pair category and RLUSD could be considered for a cash-side pair if its separate legal conditions are satisfied.
overlaps.missing: No Ripple TSV role, XRPL deployment, tokenized NMS stock pool, XRP or RLUSD selection, Covered Firm, committed or actually supplied inventory, or persistence over time is established.
overlaps.watch: A TSV notice naming XRPL, contracts or protocol functions, XRP or RLUSD pairs, liquidity providers, route share and net financed inventory.

overlaps.overlap: Securitize has relevant transfer-agent, broker-dealer/ATS, adviser and servicing bodies and disclosed multichain record models that could support stock creation, rights, admission, authoritative records and corporate actions around a TSV.
overlaps.missing: Its registrations do not make an affiliate a TSV, and registered activity must remain distinct from the exempt venue. No qualifying notice, pool or Tokenized NMS Stock is established.
overlaps.watch: Exact affiliate separation, issuer mandate, rights audit, transfer-agent control book, TSV notice, chain and settlement arrangements.

overlaps.overlap: Ethereum is a public, permissionless smart-contract network with mature AMM infrastructure and token standards, closely matching the order's technical venue surface.
overlaps.missing: Technical fit does not establish a U.S.-person TSV, permissioned participant layer, eligible stock rights, issuer process, caps, reporting, liquidity provider or legal settlement model.
overlaps.watch: Named TSV contracts, permissioning design, tokenizer and transfer agent, selected pair assets, Covered Firms and operating data.

overlaps.overlap: Hedera provides public token and smart-contract execution and has a recorded tokenized-collateral pilot relevant to asset and liquidity workflows.
overlaps.missing: The exact deployment must satisfy the order's public-permissionless DLT condition; council governance, validator admission, stock rights and qualifying AMM design require product-specific analysis.
overlaps.watch: Network and node-access facts cited in a TSV notice, contract addresses, permissioned market layer and eligible stock or pair evidence.

overlaps.overlap: Stellar is a public asset network with protocol exchange and liquidity-pool functions that could support the technical execution and non-security-asset pair surface.
overlaps.missing: No TSV operator, Tokenized NMS Stock rights package, issuer process, transfer-agent hierarchy, Covered Firm or settlement arrangement is established.
overlaps.watch: A notice naming Stellar, the exact pool implementation, asset issuers, participant admission, market data and rights servicing.

overlaps.overlap: Canton's synchronized institutional workflows, privacy controls and completed Treasury-for-USDCx event are relevant to external settlement, interoperability and institutional operations.
overlaps.missing: The tracked Canton design is permissioned institutional infrastructure rather than the order's required public, permissionless DLT application surface.
overlaps.watch: Whether a TSV uses a separate eligible public chain while connecting Canton for off-venue records, custody, liquidity or settlement.

overlaps.overlap: Solana is a public, permissionless execution network with smart contracts, token programs and active AMM infrastructure that could address the technical pool surface.
overlaps.missing: No order-specific TSV, eligible tokenized stock, issuer notice, permissioned participant set, Covered Firm, reporting or settlement chain is established.
overlaps.watch: Named venue programs, stock and pair contracts, admission controls, oracle design, liquidity inventory and operational-event handling.

overlaps.overlap: Avalanche offers a public C-Chain and configurable L1 deployments with smart-contract and AMM capability.
overlaps.missing: Eligibility turns on the exact deployment: a permissioned custom L1 cannot be assumed to satisfy the public-permissionless requirement merely because it belongs to the Avalanche family.
overlaps.watch: The chain named in a TSV notice, validator and access model, public code and contracts, pool design and external record/settlement dependencies.

overlaps.overlap: Chainlink can supply oracles, cross-chain messaging and execution support relevant to pricing, interoperability and operational controls disclosed by a TSV.
overlaps.missing: Middleware is not itself the required public-permissionless TSV base venue, tokenized stock, authoritative record, liquidity provider or settlement institution.
overlaps.watch: Named oracle feeds, CCIP routes, administrative controls, fallback rules, data incidents and their relationship to the venue's contracts.

overlaps.watch: Exact entity and affiliate separation, Base contracts, permissioning, tokenized stock rights, custody, liquidity provider and broker-dealer obligations.

overlaps.overlap: Algorand is a public, permissionless L1 with asset and smart-contract functionality that could host a qualifying application and AMM pool.
overlaps.missing: No TSV notice, eligible stock issue, issuer process, pool, participant layer, liquidity provider, reporting or legal settlement chain is established.
overlaps.watch: Named Algorand application, contracts and keys; rights and record model; pair asset; venue and Covered Firm disclosures; first operation.

overlaps.overlap: XDC's public trade-finance network, token and smart-contract functions are adjacent to tokenized-asset execution and institutional access design.
overlaps.missing: The exact validator, permissionless-deployment and AMM facts needed by the order are not established for a TSV use; trade-document roles are not Tokenized NMS Stock rights.
overlaps.watch: A notice naming XDC, public-permissionless deployment evidence, pool contracts, stock tokenizer, admission model and settlement dependencies.

overlaps.overlap: IOTA provides a public L1 and smart-contract environment, while TWIN demonstrates digital-trade-document coordination relevant to external records and identity.
overlaps.missing: No qualifying AMM venue, Tokenized NMS Stock, issuer rights, transfer-agent hierarchy, participant permissioning or market-liquidity evidence is established.
overlaps.watch: A TSV-specific public-chain deployment, smart contracts, eligible stock and pair, admission and identity layer, record authority and operating receipt.

overlaps.overlap: Wormhole could provide disclosed interoperability or transport between a TSV's selected public chain and other supported representations or applications.
overlaps.missing: A bridge is not the TSV, issuer, transfer agent, custodian, Covered Firm or legal-finality authority, and cross-chain movement can create duplicate-supply and correction questions.
overlaps.watch: Named bridge role, canonical token and burn/mint controls, authoritative supply reconciliation, pause keys, incident history and legal effect of the destination representation.

overlaps.overlap: Quant's proprietary orchestration and API model could connect regulated systems or off-chain records to a qualifying venue.
overlaps.missing: The tracked orchestration layer is not itself a public, permissionless DLT or permissioned AMM pool and does not confer stock rights, venue status or settlement finality.
overlaps.watch: A named service-provider role in a TSV notice, exact public-chain endpoint, instruction authority, data custody, reconciliation and failure responsibility.

overlaps.overlap: SWIFT's bank network and ledger work could support external messaging, funded commitments, bank conversion or settlement coordination around a TSV.
overlaps.missing: The tracked SWIFT design is controlled bank infrastructure, not the required public-permissionless AMM venue, and public terms do not establish the order's stock, pool or finality conditions.

functions.label: Supervise and authorize
functions.question: Who grants, supervises or withdraws the relevant permission?
functions.qualification_check: Statutory remit, territorial nexus, formal delegation and the entity-specific supervisory or authorization decision.

functions.label: Govern the organization or system
functions.question: Who can set rules, appoint operators or change the system?
functions.qualification_check: Constitution, bylaws, shareholder or foundation powers, system rulebook and technical upgrade controls; keep these powers distinct.

functions.label: Issuance & redemption
functions.question: Who owes the holder, and who handles issuance or redemption?
functions.qualification_check: Issuer legal identity, instrument terms, issuance authority, eligible subscribers and who may demand redemption.

functions.label: Hold the claim or registered title
functions.display_title: Hold the claim or registered title
functions.question: Who is the beneficial investor, customer, registered holder or nominee?
functions.qualification_check: Register, nominee agreement, beneficial-interest chain, client account and restrictions on eligible holders.

functions.label: Safeguard assets and keys
functions.question: Who holds assets, accounts or keys, and for whose benefit?
functions.qualification_check: Custody/subcustody contract, account title, segregation, asset eligibility, possession or control and applicable custody regime.

functions.label: Manage reserve assets
functions.question: Who chooses and manages reserves backing the claim?
functions.qualification_check: Reserve ownership, permitted investments, investment-management mandate, custody separation and reporting obligations.

functions.label: Administer a trust
functions.question: Which trustee holds title or exercises powers under the trust instrument?
functions.qualification_check: Trust instrument, trustee appointment, beneficiaries, fiduciary powers and governing law.

functions.label: Advise or manage investments
functions.question: Who advises the investor or manages the portfolio under an appointment?
functions.qualification_check: Advisory activity, jurisdiction, registration or exemption, executed mandate and applicable custody obligations.

functions.label: Admit customers and participants
functions.question: Who decides eligibility and grants access to this particular service?
functions.qualification_check: Service rulebook, onboarding authority, customer/member criteria, product and territorial restrictions.

functions.label: Participate through an account or member
functions.display_title: Participate through an account or member
functions.question: Who has direct access, and who acts through a sponsor or intermediary?
functions.qualification_check: Direct membership or sponsored-access agreement, account rights, intermediary chain and obligations on default.

functions.label: Arrange or distribute transactions
functions.question: Who effects securities transactions or distributes the investment?
functions.qualification_check: Security and activity tests, registration or exemption, client capacity and distribution/placement agreement.

functions.label: Operate a trading venue
functions.question: Who brings orders together, under which venue regime?
functions.qualification_check: Instrument and order-interaction model; exchange/ATS, DCM or SEF gateway as applicable; operating permission and participant rules.

functions.label: Instructions & transport
functions.question: Who authorizes an instruction, and who only transports it?
functions.qualification_check: Authorized signers, delegated mandate, authentication, valid instruction format and cancellation powers.

functions.label: Carry messages across systems
functions.question: Who transports a message, and who is authorized to act on it?
functions.qualification_check: Messaging/service agreement, delivery and authentication duties; receipt of a message does not establish settlement.

functions.label: Operate networks and validate updates
functions.question: Who orders, validates or operates the technical state transition?
functions.qualification_check: Identifiable operator or validator group, consensus and upgrade powers, service terms and the legal effect assigned to its records.

functions.label: Supply software and infrastructure
functions.question: Who supplies the technology, and which legal functions remain with its customer?
functions.qualification_check: Service contract, outsourced functions, accountability retained by the regulated client and access/continuity controls.

functions.label: Clearing / netting / guarantees
functions.question: Who provides clearing, netting or a counterparty guarantee?
functions.qualification_check: Clearing-agency or DCO gateway as applicable; admission, novation/netting, margin, guarantee and default rules.

functions.label: Funding and liquidity resources
functions.question: Who supplies or administers the resources the transaction needs?
functions.qualification_check: Credit or liquidity agreement, collateral, draw conditions, provider capacity, timing and loss allocation.

functions.label: Securities settlement
functions.question: Who operates the securities leg, under which account rules?
functions.qualification_check: Custody or depository chain, delivery authority, eligible instrument, account transfer and legally effective finality.

functions.label: Cash settlement
functions.question: Who operates cash settlement, and which cash obligation does it discharge?
functions.qualification_check: Settlement asset and obligor, account eligibility, system rulebook, payment discharge and insolvency protection.

functions.label: Provide payment and conversion services
functions.question: Who collects, converts or pays out customer money?
functions.qualification_check: Payment-service authorization scope, client-money treatment, collection/conversion/payout contracts and local banking access.

functions.label: Recordkeeping
functions.question: Who maintains which ownership, entitlement or account record?
functions.qualification_check: Controlling register or entitlement record, issuer appointment, applicable transfer-agent duties and reconciliation authority.

functions.label: Posting and servicing
functions.question: Who updates the books and administers continuing holder rights?
functions.qualification_check: Administration or agency appointment, corporate-action entitlement, distribution calculation and payment instructions.

functions.label: Correction, default and recovery
functions.question: Who can correct records, manage default or organize recovery?
functions.qualification_check: Error-correction mandate, reversal/freeze powers, evidentiary trail, notice requirements and loss allocation.

functions.label: Report trades and retain regulatory records
functions.display_title: Report trades and retain regulatory records
functions.question: Who must report, who submits, and which repository receives the record?
functions.qualification_check: Reporting obligation, responsible counterparty, submission delegate and relevant SDR/trade-repository regime.

functions.label: Recover or resolve a failed institution
functions.display_title: Recover or resolve a failed institution
functions.question: Who can restructure, close out, administer insolvency or resolve failure?
functions.qualification_check: Governing insolvency or resolution regime, competent authority or court, receiver/trustee powers and enforceable default arrangements.

research_gaps.detail: Recover issuer registers, nominee and beneficial-holder arrangements, custody and subcustody agreements, reserve ownership and investment mandates.

research_gaps.title: Expand trading and derivatives coverage
research_gaps.detail: Name relevant exchanges, ATSs, broker/dealers, futures commission merchants, DCMs, SEFs, DCOs and trade repositories for the products in scope.

research_gaps.title: Prove access and transaction eligibility
research_gaps.detail: Map direct members, sponsors, clients, settlement agents, account eligibility, asset eligibility and territorial restrictions separately.

research_gaps.title: Complete public-authority and failure roles
research_gaps.detail: Identify the relevant supervisor, resolution authority, court, receiver, insolvency administrator and default-management powers for each arrangement.

research_gaps.title: Separate law in force from proposals
research_gaps.detail: Track the SEC transfer-agent proposal and stablecoin implementation against effective rules; proposals and applications are not approvals.

visual_cases.title: BUIDL · subscribe and record fund shares
visual_cases.description: Follow the fund share, subscription money and official register. This maps contractual responsibilities; individual payment receipts remain unresolved.

asset.text: BUIDL is offered through the named placement and access function for eligible investors.
asset.boundary: Product-specific eligibility and offering restrictions remain controlling; placement authority is not transfer-agent authority.

money.text: The payment instruction, bank, funding account, and receipt for a particular subscription are not mapped.
money.boundary: The saved BUIDL records do not establish a subscription-payment route or completed cash posting.

record.text: Eligibility to enter an offering is documented separately from the shareholder record.
record.boundary: Admission does not by itself establish a recorded fund-share entitlement.

asset.text: The fund issuer creates shares; Securitize acts under its appointment.
asset.boundary: Manager, fund, and transfer agent are separate persons and systems.

money.text: Issuance requires confirmation of receipt or credit of subscription funds to the custodian.
money.boundary: Contractual condition in section 2.3; a particular investor’s payment receipt is not provided.

record.text: Securitize maintains the issuer’s share register.
record.boundary: The control book is distinct from a wallet, bridge, or chain consensus record.

asset.text: BUIDL has named live representations on supported networks, including Ethereum.
asset.boundary: Network availability is not proof that a network is the exclusive or legally authoritative register.

money.text: No network representation establishes a subscription payment or cash settlement path.
money.boundary: The saved evidence does not link the representation to a particular money movement.

record.text: Securitize's multichain model uses Wormhole infrastructure while the regulated control book remains external to transport.
record.boundary: Transport does not replace the transfer-agent record or determine legal title.

asset.text: Ongoing BUIDL share servicing remains governed by the reviewed transfer-agent agreement.
asset.boundary: The terms and required instructions determine whether a transfer is recognized.

money.text: Cash redemption route and payout completion for this case are not documented here.
money.boundary: The case does not treat a separate RLUSD exchange option as a subscription or fiat-payout proof.

record.text: Securitize may refuse a transfer lacking valid authority.
record.boundary: Contract sections 3.2–3.5 address transfer instructions and adverse claims; network consensus is not that authorization.

visual_cases.title: USDC · issue, transfer and redeem
visual_cases.description: Follow the token, reserve money and issuer records. Direct redemption depends on customer eligibility; token movement does not prove bank payout.

asset.text: Circle Mint provides the access path for an eligible institution to seek issuance of USDC.
asset.boundary: KYC and service access are mapped; a particular bank-funding instruction and posting receipt are absent.

money.text: A specific incoming USD payment route or settlement receipt is not mapped.
money.boundary: Access eligibility does not prove bank funding, reserve receipt, or final settlement of a given order.

record.text: The applicable legal issuer is the issuer-side liability and instruction authority for USDC.
record.boundary: The issuer perimeter remains distinct from Circle Mint access and from every supported network.

asset.text: Native USDC is minted under issuer instruction on a selected supported chain.
asset.boundary: This generic trace does not specify the selected-chain execution for a particular issuance.

money.text: Dollar assets enter an issuer-specific segregated reserve pool.
money.boundary: The reserve-pool role is mapped, not a transaction-level reserve inflow posting.

record.text: The issuer's USDC obligation and reserve records remain separate from token state.
record.boundary: Chain state does not itself establish the issuer liability or reserve position.

asset.text: USDC can move through wallets and supported transport mechanisms.
asset.boundary: The mechanisms are alternatives, not successive mandatory hops in one transaction.

money.text: No token transfer alone establishes an FX conversion, bank payout, or new fiat settlement.
money.boundary: Token transport is not evidence of completed money movement outside the issuer claim.

record.text: Technical token state and transport are distinct from the issuer liability record and redemption eligibility.
record.boundary: Chain finality does not guarantee direct Circle redemption eligibility.

asset.text: USDC is burned under applicable issuer eligibility rules when redeemed.
asset.boundary: No transaction-specific burn receipt is supplied.

money.text: Reserve liquidity is intended to become bank USD payout, but a separate direct-Circle payout completion card is not mapped.
money.boundary: Do not use a distinct Tazapay conversion/local-payout route to fill this direct-redemption gap.

record.text: Issuer redemption terms govern the obligation; token burn and bank payout remain distinct evidence points.
record.boundary: Burn does not by itself prove completed bank payout or discharge for a specific customer.

visual_cases.title: Coinbase certificate · underlying share to registered title
visual_cases.description: Follow the underlying share, issued certificate and controlling register. Wallet possession and registered ownership are distinct.

asset.text: An Authorized Participant submits the current in-kind creation order for the certificate process.
asset.boundary: Eligibility is mapped, but acceptance of a particular in-kind creation instruction lacks a dedicated card.

money.text: This is an in-kind underlying-security creation case; no cash payment route is mapped.
money.boundary: The saved trace does not establish a cash-leg settlement for an individual creation.

record.text: Certificate eligibility and later vesting gates are distinct from wallet possession.
record.boundary: Admission does not itself establish registered ownership.

asset.text: AAPL enters the issuer-named Alpaca custody account; Coinbase Onchain SPV holds deposited property on trust and legally issues the certificate.
asset.boundary: The certificate is not direct ownership of the underlying U.S. share, and the underlying company does not sponsor it.

money.text: No cash purchase, securities-loan, or cash-settlement instruction is documented for this stage.
money.boundary: Custody and certificate issuance do not prove a separate cash leg.

record.text: The SPV-issued certificate is a distinct legal object against deposited underlying property.
record.boundary: Underlying custody is separate from certificate issuance, wallet possession, and Base state.

asset.text: The B20 certificate is represented on Base.
asset.boundary: Legal issuance and Base representation are mapped; the OML-specific mint action is not separately recorded.

money.text: Base transaction ordering and Ethereum settlement do not identify a cash settlement.
money.boundary: Sequencer ordering and Ethereum finality do not determine certificate cash settlement.

record.text: Wallet control creates an onchain position, while OML separately applies eligibility and vesting checks.
record.boundary: Wallet possession alone does not establish registered title.

asset.text: Certificate rights, including redemption and voting eligibility, depend on registered and vested status.
asset.boundary: Unvested holders lack the documented redemption and voting rights.

money.text: A cash redemption or payout route is not established by the certificate or its Base representation.
money.boundary: The trace does not supply a dedicated redemption/burn execution or cash-settlement action.

record.text: OML operates the definitive Legal Register; registered entry and vesting determine certificate title.
record.boundary: The Legal Register, rather than Base state or wallet possession alone, controls title and servicing.

market_overview.boundary: Navigation projection over existing research, not a new legal taxonomy or a complete market census.

layers.title: Public authority
layers.question: Who sets the rules and grants permission?
layers.gap: Use the institutional map above for sourced public-authority relationships.

layers.title: Claims and ownership
layers.question: Who owes the holder, and what does the holder own?
layers.gap: Resolve beneficial ownership, reserve ownership and the exact investment or trust mandate.

layers.title: Market access and connections
layers.question: Who admits participants, executes orders or runs the connection?
layers.gap: Identify direct versus sponsored access and distinguish legal authorization from technical connectivity.

layers.title: Records and custody
layers.question: Which record controls the right, and who safeguards the assets?
layers.gap: Recover custody/subcustody terms and reconcile the issuer register, entitlement records and wallet state.

layers.title: Funding and settlement
layers.question: Who provides resources, clears obligations and settles each leg?
layers.gap: Prove account access, payment asset, funding conditions and the legal point of finality.

layers.title: Servicing and failure
layers.question: Who services the position, corrects errors and allocates loss?
layers.gap: Identify the governing default, insolvency and resolution powers for the exact entity and jurisdiction.

infrastructure_map.scope: Active research focus: U.S. law, regulators, market infrastructure, access and private roles. International standards and directly connected arrangements provide context; inclusion does not imply U.S. domicile or U.S. authorization. Saved foreign-jurisdiction research remains available through the jurisdiction selector.

entities.label: U.S. Congress
entities.scope: Enacts federal statutes. Agency powers must be traced to the relevant statute.
entities.boundary: No edge here assigns Congress day-to-day supervision of a market institution.
entities.evidence_date: Retrieved 2026-09-10; source retains its own date

entities.label: U.S. Department of the Treasury
entities.scope: Federal department; its Secretary chairs FSOC.
entities.boundary: Treasury chairmanship of FSOC does not make Treasury the operating supervisor of every FSOC-member agency or utility.
entities.evidence_date: Retrieved 2026-09-10; source retains its own date

entities.label: Financial Stability Oversight Council
entities.scope: Statutory financial-stability coordination body; can designate systemically important FMUs or payment, clearing, or settlement activities under Title VIII.
entities.boundary: Its membership and designation powers do not consolidate its members' ordinary statutory jurisdictions.
entities.evidence_date: Retrieved 2026-09-10; source retains its own date

entities.label: Office of Financial Research
entities.scope: FSOC support/data office; its Director is an FSOC nonvoting member.
entities.boundary: This map does not treat OFR as a prudential supervisor or market operator.
entities.evidence_date: Retrieved 2026-09-10; source retains its own date

entities.label: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
entities.scope: Federal agency governing the Federal Reserve System; oversees the 12 Reserve Banks and shares supervision/regulation responsibilities for specified institutions and activities.
entities.boundary: Board oversight of Reserve Banks differs from every Reserve Bank's operations and from FSOC coordination.
entities.evidence_date: Retrieved 2026-09-10; source retains its own date

entities.label: 12 Federal Reserve Banks
entities.scope: Federal Reserve operating arms: provide accounts and services to depository institutions and fiscal-agent services to the U.S. government; perform other System functions.
entities.boundary: They do not provide banking services or accounts to individuals; shared System roles do not erase separate legal and operating roles.
entities.evidence_date: Retrieved 2026-09-10; source retains its own date

entities.label: Federal Open Market Committee
entities.scope: Federal Reserve monetary-policymaking body.
entities.boundary: Monetary-policy authority is distinct from prudential supervision, market registration, and payment-system operation.
entities.evidence_date: Retrieved 2026-09-10; source retains its own date

entities.label: Securities and Exchange Commission
entities.scope: Federal securities-market regulator, including registration, regulation, and oversight of clearing agencies and securities SROs.
entities.boundary: SEC oversight of an SRO or clearing agency does not make the SEC the entity's market operator or a banking supervisor.
entities.evidence_date: Retrieved 2026-09-10; source retains its own date

entities.label: SEC-registered clearing agencies
entities.scope: Securities clearing-agency category registered with or exempted by the SEC under Exchange Act Section 17A and related rules.
entities.boundary: A clearing agency may perform CCP or CSD functions; this category is not a blanket label for all payment or ledger services.
entities.evidence_date: Retrieved 2026-09-10; source retains its own date

entities.label: Financial Industry Regulatory Authority
entities.scope: Securities SRO and the only registered national securities association identified by the SEC source.
entities.boundary: FINRA is not a federal agency and does not replace the SEC's statutory authority.
entities.evidence_date: Retrieved 2026-09-10; source retains its own date

entities.label: Commodity Futures Trading Commission
entities.scope: Federal derivatives regulator; reviews applications for derivatives clearing organization registration and supervises NFA's delegated intermediary work.

entities.evidence_date: Retrieved 2026-09-10; source retains its own date

entities.label: CFTC-registered derivatives clearing organizations
entities.scope: DCO category registered under Commodity Exchange Act section 5b and CFTC Part 39.

entities.evidence_date: Retrieved 2026-09-10; source retains its own date

entities.label: National Futures Association
entities.scope: CFTC-designated registered futures association; performs delegated registration and examination of intermediaries.

entities.evidence_date: Retrieved 2026-09-10; source retains its own date

entities.scope: Independent Treasury bureau that charters, regulates, and supervises national banks, federal savings associations, and federal branches/agencies of foreign banks.
