steps_rights_hub.title: Steps & rights
steps_rights_hub.scope: U.S. current-system walkthroughs with dated crypto overlays. These are representative routes, not one universal market sequence.

statuses.label: Specified capability
statuses.meaning: The cited source specifies this bounded function; it is not proof every transaction works.

statuses.label: Continuing dependency
statuses.meaning: The function still relies on a legal entity, account, contract, funding source or remedy.

statuses.label: Evidence gap
statuses.meaning: The saved evidence does not establish this link. Absence of evidence does not prove impossibility.

statuses.label: Outside reviewed design
statuses.meaning: This function is outside the cited architecture; that does not mean no future design could supply it.

routes.title: Buy a broker-held security
routes.baseline: A secondary-market purchase routed through NSCC CNS and DTC
routes.scope: An eligible U.S. broker-to-broker cash-security trade. Not every security or trade uses CNS; direct registration, primary issuance, Treasuries and derivatives have different routes. Customer, clearing-member and depository records are separate.
routes.clock: Current conventional service model; crypto comparison uses the December 11, 2025 conditional no-action architecture. The letter is not a production receipt or Commission approval.
chain: Clearing member ↔ NSCC: accepted CNS obligations
Cede ↔ issuer / transfer agent: registered holding

steps.title: Open the right account
steps.action: The investor establishes a brokerage account and chooses how the security will be held.
steps.actors: Investor; broker; carrying or clearing firm.
steps.right: Account rights and an instruction relationship exist. Opening an account does not itself acquire a security.
steps.proof: Identify the carrying entity, holding method and permitted activity.
steps.crypto: The reviewed DTC design adds participant-linked registered wallets; it does not give any wallet owner direct DTC membership.
steps.gap: Access remains institution-controlled.
steps.needed: For a named user, recover the broker-to-participant and wallet authorization chain.

steps.title: Execute and confirm the trade
steps.action: The broker obtains execution; trade details establish the agreed security, quantity, price and settlement terms.
steps.actors: Buyer and seller through brokers; trading venue where used.
steps.right: A trade obligation is created. Execution is not evidence that delivery and payment have finished.
steps.record: Execution report and confirmation; allocation / affirmation records where applicable.
steps.proof: Match instrument, quantity, price, parties and intended settlement date. The standard T+1 rule has exceptions.
steps.crypto: A token transfer facility does not establish a trading venue, broker mandate or execution receipt.
steps.gap: End-to-end execution is not supplied by this tokenization letter.
steps.needed: Link the actual venue and execution record to the later token movement.

steps.title: Clear and prepare resources
steps.action: For eligible accepted CNS trades, NSCC becomes the central counterparty and nets positions by security and member. Members supply required resources.
steps.actors: NSCC; clearing members; funding providers.
steps.right: Member obligations to the CCP replace the covered bilateral obligations under the applicable rules. This is a different relationship from the customer account.
steps.record: CNS positions and member risk / funding records.
steps.proof: Establish acceptance, the applicable guarantee point, net obligations and required resources.
steps.crypto: Token movement does not by itself provide CNS novation, margin or a default guarantee.
steps.gap: Risk-bearing capacity remains a separate service.
steps.needed: Identify any clearing arrangement or document that the trade is bilateral and how its risks are handled.

steps.title: Deliver securities and settle cash
steps.action: DTC processes participant securities movements; money obligations follow its settlement arrangements and settling-bank rules.
steps.actors: DTC participants; DTC; NSCC where used; settling banks.
steps.right: Securities entitlements and payment obligations change at their applicable rule-defined events. A securities entry alone does not prove all cash obligations discharged.
steps.record: DTC securities positions; money-settlement and bank records.
steps.proof: Obtain both legs, account identities and the applicable finality provisions.
steps.crypto: The letter describes token entitlement transfers without a DTC-run value leg, and contemplates any associated DvP away from DTC. It supplies no receipt for such a cash arrangement.
steps.gap: An integrated DTC token cash leg is outside the reviewed architecture.
steps.needed: Name the external cash asset, operator, funding and enforceable linkage between the two legs.
steps.source_note: The saved DTC Rules URL failed direct retrieval in the institutional audit; exact current clauses and any later amendments remain to be recovered.

steps.title: Credit the holder’s record
steps.action: The broker maintains the customer holding; DTC maintains participant entitlements; the issuer register can continue to name Cede.
steps.actors: Broker; DTC participant; DTC; issuer / transfer agent.
steps.right: The customer’s entitlement is assessed at its own intermediary tier. New York §8-501 gives acquisition conditions, including book-entry credit; it need not wait for that intermediary to obtain the asset.
steps.record: Customer securities account → participant account → issuer register.
steps.proof: Reconcile each tier. Do not treat a retail account statement as an entry in the issuer register.
steps.crypto: LedgerScan is the official DTC record for tokenized entitlements in the reviewed design; Cede stays registered holder.
steps.gap: The record function is specified; each customer’s downstream record still needs reconciliation.
steps.needed: Obtain a matched token, LedgerScan and customer-account example for the named arrangement.

steps.title: Exercise rights, exit or resolve a problem
steps.action: Intermediaries handle distributions and valid entitlement orders. Sale, transfer and a failure claim follow different procedures.
steps.actors: Holder; broker; issuer / agent; relevant court or receiver on failure.
steps.right: Rights to distributions and compliance with qualifying orders depend on law and agreement. A market-value loss is not automatically a compensable custody failure.
steps.record: Distribution records, entitlement orders, account terms and any claims proceeding.
steps.proof: Identify who must act, the conditions, deadline and available remedy.
steps.crypto: DTC retains correction and conversion controls in the reviewed token design. Immutability does not remove that authority.
steps.gap: Legal servicing and remedies continue alongside the token.
steps.needed: Recover current correction terms and holder-level recovery rights; do not infer a payout from a token balance.

routes.title: Subscribe to a fund
routes.baseline: An issuer-led subscription, recordkeeping and redemption workflow
routes.scope: A terms-based fund workflow, not the exchange-trade route above. BUIDL is a U.S.-connected example with an offshore fund issuer; it is not a template for every U.S. fund or a conclusion about investor eligibility.
routes.clock: Filed BUIDL agreement dated March 14, 2024, read September 10, 2026. Offering-document terms and later amendments are not all supplied. Separate network announcements retain their dates.
chain: Investor ↔ fund issuer: share rights under fund terms
Fund ↔ transfer agent / registrar: delegated recordkeeping
Fund ↔ custodian: assets supporting the portfolio
Token / wallet ↔ share record: product-specific linkage

steps.title: Establish eligibility and submit
steps.action: The prospective investor supplies the subscription documents required by the issue.
steps.actors: Investor; issuer; onboarding and transfer-agent service providers.
steps.right: An application is not yet an unconditional shareholding or a promise of admission.
steps.record: Offering terms, subscription documents and eligibility decision.
steps.proof: Recover the current investor category, jurisdiction, minimum and acceptance conditions.
steps.crypto: Securitize’s filed BUIDL contract ties platform access to issue documentation and compliance checks.
steps.gap: A compatible wallet does not satisfy investment eligibility.
steps.needed: Read the current offering memorandum and the named investor’s acceptance.

steps.title: Confirm subscription funding
steps.action: The subscription requires confirmation of funds at the issuer’s custodian under the issue terms.
steps.actors: Investor; funding bank; issuer’s custodian; transfer agent.
steps.right: Sending money and acquiring shares are separate events; rejected or incomplete subscriptions need their own treatment.
steps.proof: Match received funds to the accepted subscription and allocation.
steps.crypto: The contract conditions share credit on documentation and funding confirmation. A mint transaction alone is insufficient proof.
steps.gap: External funding confirmation remains part of the workflow.
steps.needed: Establish the accepted cash asset, receipt, cutoffs and refund treatment for this subscription.

steps.title: Issue shares and record the holder
steps.action: The appointed agent records the shareholding pursuant to the issuer’s instructions and governing terms.
steps.actors: Issuer; transfer agent and registrar; admitted investor.
steps.right: The investor receives fund-share rights, not direct title to each portfolio asset.
steps.record: Issuer’s shareholder records and issue-specific digital representation.
steps.proof: Tie the share class, quantity and investor identity to the recognized holding.
steps.crypto: The BUIDL agreement appoints Securitize as registrar and includes blockchain representations.
steps.gap: The mapping is product-specific, not universal token title.
steps.needed: Match the current share register to a named wallet and reconcile any discrepancy.

steps.title: Transfer to an eligible recipient
steps.action: A transfer request must satisfy the issue’s transfer conditions before the recognized holding changes.
steps.actors: Transferor; transferee; issuer / transfer agent.
steps.right: Technical delivery and an authorized transfer of fund-share rights must be connected by the issue’s rules.
steps.record: Authorized transfer and updated shareholder record.
steps.proof: Verify recipient eligibility and the agent’s recognized record update.
steps.crypto: Saved BUIDL network disclosures describe digital transfer support. Network availability does not establish approval for every recipient.
steps.gap: A particular transfer still needs legal and operational evidence.
steps.needed: Obtain the approved transfer workflow and matched records on both sides.

steps.title: Redeem and receive payment
steps.action: Apply the offering terms to a redemption request, share cancellation and payment.
steps.actors: Investor; issuer; transfer agent; custodian / paying bank.
steps.right: Redemption rights depend on fund terms. A request, token burn and received cash are distinct evidence points.
steps.record: Redemption acceptance, cancelled shares and payment receipt.
steps.proof: Verify eligibility, timing, valuation, any suspension terms and actual payout.
steps.crypto: The filed service scope includes redemption burns and USD payment. This is a contractual assignment, not evidence of a completed redemption or cash receipt.
steps.gap: Liquidity and enforceable redemption remain issuer obligations under the terms.
steps.needed: Recover the current redemption conditions and a completed payout record.

routes.title: Make a dollar payment
routes.baseline: A bank-to-bank dollar transfer using Fedwire Funds
routes.scope: Compare outcomes, not identical instruments: a bank deposit and USDC have different obligors and terms. This Fedwire example is not a universal route for ACH, card payments, internal bank transfers or every retail transfer. Regulation J has scope exclusions. New York Article 4-A supplies a scoped rights example; its applicability is not presumed for every transfer.
routes.clock: OC 6 effective January 5, 2026; Regulation J and Circle terms checked September 10. Contractual rights are distinct from a receipt for a specific payment.
chain: Payer ↔ payer bank: deposit and instruction relationship
Sending bank ↔ Reserve Bank service: covered payment order
Beneficiary bank ↔ beneficiary: receiving account obligation
USDC alternative: holder ↔ applicable issuer / intermediary

steps.title: Identify what the payer holds
steps.action: Identify the sending account, bank and intended beneficiary before giving payment instructions.
steps.actors: Payer; payer bank; intended beneficiary.
steps.right: A bank-account claim and the obligation being paid are different relationships.
steps.record: Account terms and the contract or invoice being paid.
steps.proof: Name the debtor, creditor, currency and acceptable means of payment.
steps.crypto: USDC is a separate issuer-linked asset; its terms are not bank-deposit terms.
steps.gap: Changing the payment asset changes the claim being held.
steps.needed: Confirm that the recipient agrees to accept USDC and on what discharge terms.

steps.title: Authorize and accept the instruction
steps.action: The customer instructs its bank; the participating bank submits a covered payment order subject to service controls.
steps.actors: Authorized customer; bank; Reserve Bank service.
steps.right: An instruction may be rejected; sending it is not the same as acceptance or completed payment.
steps.record: Authenticated order, acceptance / rejection and account identifiers.
steps.proof: Verify authorized sender, recipient and the order’s processing state.
steps.crypto: A wallet signature authorizes a token instruction under its controls; it is not a bank payment order.
steps.gap: Token instruction is a different mechanism.
steps.needed: Check custody, signing authority, correct token contract and recipient network.

steps.title: Provide the resources
steps.action: The sending institution must meet applicable account and funding conditions.
steps.actors: Sending bank; liquidity or credit provider; Reserve Bank.
steps.right: A payment message does not supply spendable funds or unlimited credit.
steps.record: Available account resources and applicable credit terms.
steps.proof: Identify funding amount, availability and any credit conditions.
steps.crypto: The sender needs transferable USDC and transaction resources; issuer reserves are not a holder’s transaction account.
steps.gap: Funding and issuer backing remain separate.
steps.needed: Verify available tokens, restrictions and any intermediary funding exposure.

steps.title: Complete the service transfer
steps.action: Reserve Banks process the covered order under Regulation J and OC 6.
steps.actors: Sending institution; Reserve Banks; receiving institution.
steps.right: Service-level payment and finality follow the applicable rules; customer payout is a separate evidence point.
steps.record: Processed order and relevant service/account records.
steps.proof: Identify the exact event that establishes payment under the service rules.
steps.crypto: A USDC transfer changes token holdings. It does not produce a Fedwire settlement receipt.
steps.gap: Central-bank settlement is outside a standalone USDC transfer.
steps.needed: If dollar-bank settlement is required, identify and document that additional leg.

steps.title: Establish what the recipient received
steps.action: Trace the receiving bank’s obligation and customer-account treatment under applicable law and terms.
steps.actors: Beneficiary bank; beneficiary; original payer.
steps.right: Where New York Article 4-A applies, §4-A-404 generally obliges an accepting beneficiary bank to pay the beneficiary. Section 4-A-406 links payment by the originator to bank acceptance and addresses underlying-debt discharge, subject to its conditions and exceptions. Actual customer availability is a separate fact.
steps.record: Beneficiary account record plus the underlying payment agreement.
steps.proof: Reconcile the bank receipt, customer credit and debt-discharge condition.
steps.crypto: A recipient can hold USDC without being eligible for direct Circle redemption.
steps.gap: Holding the token does not guarantee direct issuer access.
steps.needed: Determine whether the recipient holds USDC, an exchange claim or spendable bank dollars.

steps.title: Convert, redeem or resolve failure
steps.action: For a bank payment, investigate errors under the governing transfer and account rules. An asset-conversion route has additional steps.
steps.actors: Customer; banks; issuer or intermediary for USDC; dispute authority.
steps.right: Redemption, market sale and an error claim are different rights against different parties.
steps.record: Redemption / exchange agreement, payout receipt or dispute record.
steps.proof: Name the responsible entity and the condition for obtaining the requested result.
steps.crypto: Direct Circle redemption requires eligibility and a Circle Mint account under its terms. Exchange sale is another route.
steps.gap: Bank payout and remedies remain outside token consensus.
steps.needed: Establish the actual exit provider, fees, restrictions, payout timing and loss allocation.

transaction_maps.title: Transaction maps

routes.title: Buy a broker-held security
routes.scope: Illustrative broker-held U.S. security, eligible for NSCC CNS and DTC. Other holding and settlement routes differ.

label: 1 · Ask to buy
nodes.before: You have an account and funds or agreed credit. You have not acquired the security merely by opening the account.
nodes.after: Your broker has a customer instruction to act on, subject to its terms.
nodes.explain: You give the broker an order. The broker acts for the customer; this does not give the customer direct clearinghouse or depository access.
nodes.overlay: A registered wallet is an additional controlled access point, not automatic DTC membership.

label: 2 · Trade agreed
nodes.before: There is an instruction, but no matched trade is established by that instruction alone.
nodes.after: Execution establishes a trade obligation for the agreed quantity, price and settlement terms.
nodes.explain: The broker obtains execution. A confirmation describes the deal; it is not a receipt for completed securities delivery and payment.
nodes.overlay: The DTC token service does not supply the trading venue or the execution receipt.

label: 3 · Obligations netted
nodes.before: Eligible trade obligations have been submitted for clearing.
nodes.after: For accepted CNS activity, members face NSCC under its rules, with net positions and resource requirements.
nodes.explain: NSCC becomes the central counterparty for the covered activity. Netting reduces deliveries; it does not remove the need for resources or default rules.
nodes.overlay: Moving an entitlement token does not create a CCP guarantee, margin or funding.

label: 4 · Securities entry
nodes.before: Participants have securities-delivery obligations and positions to deliver.
nodes.after: The applicable DTC entry changes participant securities positions; cash and customer records still require their own evidence.
nodes.explain: DTC transfers securities interests by entries in participant records. This is an institutional tier, not a direct rewrite of every investor’s account.
nodes.overlay: DTC’s reviewed architecture adds tokenized entitlements and LedgerScan here. The issuer register continues to name Cede.

label: 5 · Money settlement
nodes.before: Participants have payment obligations and must arrange the required money resources.
nodes.after: Money obligations are settled under the applicable arrangements when the required rule-defined events occur.
nodes.explain: Settling banks support the money side. We need a cash receipt as well as a securities receipt; one alone does not prove the full transaction completed.
nodes.overlay: The reviewed tokenization design does not provide a DTC-run value leg. An associated cash or DvP arrangement must be evidenced separately.

label: 6 · Customer record
nodes.before: Customer rights and institutional records may be at different points in processing.
nodes.after: The customer’s securities account records the holding at its own intermediary tier.
nodes.explain: The customer looks to the carrying intermediary’s records. Entitlement acquisition can occur before that intermediary actually obtains the asset; this teaching order is not a universal legal clock.
nodes.overlay: A LedgerScan entry concerns a DTC participant. A matched customer-account record is still needed.

label: 7 · Hold / instruct
nodes.before: The customer has a holding with rights governed by the instrument, account and applicable law.
nodes.after: Distributions, transfer instructions and later sales are exercised through the relevant arrangements.
nodes.explain: Owning through an intermediary gives a different record relationship from direct registration. A request to sell or transfer starts another process.
nodes.overlay: Servicing, corrections and legal remedies remain assigned to institutions; token possession does not remove those duties.

label: Register · unchanged
Cede stays named
nodes.before: The issuer register identifies the registered holder for the deposited position.
nodes.after: An ordinary participant or customer transfer need not change that registered holder.
nodes.explain: This is a continuing ownership-record relationship, not an eighth transaction step. Cede, the DTC participant and the customer must not be collapsed into one holder.
nodes.overlay: In the reviewed DTC token design, Cede remains registered holder. Tokenization does not turn the wallet owner into the issuer’s registered shareholder.

routes.subtitle: Follow a securities purchase from order to holding
routes.footprint: Adds a tokenized form of the DTC participant entitlement and its record. Trading, risk resources, the cash leg and customer records still need their own arrangements.
routes.timing: Customer entitlements may arise before the intermediary receives the asset. Securities delivery and money settlement have separate completion events.
routes.boundary: Illustrative eligible CNS/DTC route. Seller-side detail and intermediary chains are summarized. The issuer register remains continuing context.

scenarios.title: Required money funding is missing
scenarios.before: The settling participant has a money obligation, but the required funding is not established.
scenarios.after: We cannot mark the cash leg complete. Identify the responsible participant or settling bank, applicable deadline and rule-governed response.
scenarios.explain: This is a hypothetical funding shortfall, not a documented incident. Existing securities entries are not automatically reversed. A delay, rejection, credit facility or default response depends on the exact rules and timing.
scenarios.overlay: A successful token movement does not fill the funding gap. Identify the external cash provider and show that the money leg completed.

scenarios.title: Customer and institutional records disagree
scenarios.before: The customer holding and the institutional position have not been reconciled.
scenarios.after: Identify the governing record at each tier and resolve the discrepancy under the relevant duties; do not assume either screen alone resolves ownership.
scenarios.explain: Hypothetical record mismatch. Customer and participant records describe different relationships. A missing or conflicting record needs investigation, not an automatic conclusion that the customer has no right.
scenarios.overlay: A token balance alone does not resolve a broker-account discrepancy. Obtain the wallet, LedgerScan and customer-account records.

label: Tokenized entitlement
overlay_nodes.before: A participant holds an eligible book-entry entitlement.
overlay_nodes.after: Under the reviewed design it can be represented as a tokenized entitlement with DTC’s record controls.
overlay_nodes.explain: This is a permitted-design comparison, not an event required in the ordinary securities route. The underlying registered holding remains separate.
overlay_nodes.overlay: DTC records tokenized participant entitlements through LedgerScan.

label: Registered-wallet move
overlay_nodes.before: A participant’s tokenized entitlement is associated with a registered wallet.
overlay_nodes.after: The reviewed design tracks transfer to another registered wallet in the DTC entitlement record.
overlay_nodes.explain: Token movement concerns this specified entitlement structure; customer postings and cash remain separate evidence.
overlay_nodes.overlay: Transfer and record tracking are described; no DTC-run value leg is supplied.

label: Convert back
overlay_nodes.before: The participant holds the tokenized form.
overlay_nodes.after: The reviewed detokenization process burns tokens and restores the book-entry form under DTC controls.
overlay_nodes.explain: This is a conversion of representation under the reviewed design, not a redemption of the underlying security for cash.
overlay_nodes.overlay: DTC’s conversion and correction authority remain.

routes.title: Subscribe to a fund
routes.subtitle: From subscription request to fund-share rights
routes.scope: Issuer-led fund workflow. BUIDL is a U.S.-connected comparison with an offshore issuer; it is not a template for every domestic fund.
routes.footprint: Adds digital representations and transfer services around a fund issue. The issuer, registrar, eligibility conditions, custodian and payment obligations remain.
routes.timing: Issuance depends on the issue terms and funding confirmation. Transfer and redemption are later branches, not mandatory steps after every subscription.
routes.boundary: The filed BUIDL agreement is dated March 14, 2024. Current offering terms and later amendments are not all supplied; contract scope does not prove a completed subscription.

label: 1 · Apply to invest
nodes.before: You are a prospective investor; submitting documents is not share ownership.
nodes.after: The issue’s eligibility and acceptance process can assess the application.
nodes.explain: The investor supplies the required materials. Eligibility, acceptance and share issuance are distinct decisions.
nodes.overlay: The platform applies issue-specific access and compliance checks; having a wallet is not admission.

label: 2 · Admission review
nodes.before: The issuer has an application to consider.
nodes.after: An accepted investor can proceed only under the offering’s current conditions.
nodes.explain: The issuer and appointed providers apply the offering rules. There is no universal entitlement to subscribe.
nodes.overlay: BUIDL eligibility follows its documentation; a network deployment does not widen the offering.

label: 3 · Funds confirmed
nodes.before: A transfer instruction may exist, but funds received for this order are not yet established.
nodes.after: The custodian-side funding confirmation supports the subscription workflow.
nodes.explain: The cash receipt must match the subscription. Funding is a separate event from a token mint or a share credit.
nodes.overlay: The BUIDL contract conditions share credit on good-form documents and funds confirmation.

label: 4 · Issue the shares
nodes.before: Subscription conditions and funding must be met.
nodes.after: The appointed agent issues and credits shares under the issuer’s instructions and issue terms.
nodes.explain: The legal actor issues fund-share rights. These are not direct ownership of each asset in the portfolio.
nodes.overlay: Securitize is appointed transfer agent and registrar; the contract includes digital representations.

label: 5 · Record the holder
nodes.before: Share issuance must be reflected in the issuer-recognized record.
nodes.after: The record identifies the investor’s holding in the relevant share class.
nodes.explain: The share register connects the legal investor to its holding. A wallet representation needs that product-specific connection.
nodes.overlay: The named registrar remains responsible; a chain balance is not a universal share register.

label: 6 · Authorized transfer
nodes.before: A holder wants to transfer; a new recipient may not yet be eligible.
nodes.after: A permitted transfer and recognized record update establish the changed holding under the terms.
nodes.explain: This is an optional branch after issuance. The transfer must satisfy the issue’s conditions.
nodes.overlay: Digital transfer support does not establish approval of every recipient or network route.

label: 7 · Request redemption
nodes.before: The investor holds shares and seeks an exit.
nodes.after: An eligible request enters the issue’s redemption process; cash receipt still needs evidence.
nodes.explain: Redemption is governed by fund terms. It differs from selling shares to another investor.
nodes.overlay: A redemption burn is one servicing event, not proof of bank payout.

label: 8 · Cancellation & pay
nodes.before: An accepted redemption still requires the applicable cancellation and payment actions.
nodes.after: The cancelled position and actual payout can be reconciled to the request.
nodes.explain: Obtain both the share-side record and cash receipt. Timing and any restrictions remain offering-specific.
nodes.overlay: The filed service scope assigns redemption burns and USD payment; that assignment is not an operating receipt.

scenarios.title: Investor eligibility is not established
scenarios.before: The application or recipient eligibility is incomplete or fails an applicable condition.
scenarios.after: Do not mark the subscription or transfer as admitted. Identify the unmet condition and authorized decision-maker.
scenarios.explain: Hypothetical admission problem. A completed wallet setup does not cure missing eligibility. Rejection, further documentation or another permitted route depends on the actual offering.
scenarios.overlay: A token interface cannot grant investment permission that the issue’s terms do not provide.

scenarios.title: Burn or cancellation recorded; payout unproven
scenarios.before: A share-side cancellation or burn is visible, but a matching cash receipt is missing.
scenarios.after: Reconcile the redemption request, cancellation, payment instruction and received funds before marking the exit complete.
scenarios.explain: Hypothetical incomplete redemption evidence. Do not infer cash receipt from cancellation, or infer default solely from an unexplained timing gap.
scenarios.overlay: Blockchain confirmation proves neither bank availability nor performance of the issuer’s payment obligation.

label: Digital representation
overlay_nodes.before: A share issue has legal and funding conditions.
overlay_nodes.after: The agreement permits a digital representation alongside the appointed registrar’s duties.
overlay_nodes.explain: The wallet representation needs a product-specific link to the recognized shareholding.
overlay_nodes.overlay: The contract supplies this digital servicing role, not a universal title rule.

label: Permitted wallet move
overlay_nodes.before: A holder seeks a digital transfer.
overlay_nodes.after: The permitted workflow must match the recipient and recognized share record.
overlay_nodes.explain: Network support does not prove eligibility or successful transfer for a particular recipient.
overlay_nodes.overlay: A matched record and permitted recipient remain necessary.

label: Redemption burn
overlay_nodes.before: A redemption-related digital action is due under the terms.
overlay_nodes.after: A burn may be recorded; payment needs a separate receipt.
overlay_nodes.explain: A burn is not the investor’s bank-dollar receipt.
overlay_nodes.overlay: Contractual servicing scope is not proof of payout.

routes.title: Make a dollar payment
routes.subtitle: From bank instruction to the recipient’s claim
routes.scope: A bank-to-bank dollar payment using Fedwire Funds. USDC is a comparison involving a different asset and obligor, not a required part of Fedwire.
routes.footprint: USDC supplies a transferable token claim. Issuer redemption eligibility, intermediary claims, bank payout and the original debt’s discharge remain separate questions.
routes.timing: Bank acceptance, service payment, customer availability and debt discharge are distinct events. Regulation J has scope exclusions; New York Article 4-A is a scoped rights example.
routes.boundary: OC 6 effective January 5, 2026 and Circle terms checked September 10. Not a universal ACH, card, retail or cross-border payment model.

label: 1 · Agree what is owed
nodes.before: The payer has a deposit claim and a separate obligation to the recipient.
nodes.after: The parties identify the amount, recipient, currency and acceptable payment method.
nodes.explain: The asset in the payer’s account and the debt being paid are different legal relationships.
nodes.overlay: USDC changes the asset and issuer relationship. Recipient acceptance of that payment method must be established.

label: 2 · Authorize the order
nodes.before: Customer intent alone is not an accepted covered payment order.
nodes.after: The bank has an instruction to accept, reject or process under its controls.
nodes.explain: Identify the authorized sender and exact account and beneficiary details. Transmission alone does not prove acceptance.
nodes.overlay: A wallet signature is not a bank payment order; custody and signing authority remain separate.

label: 3 · Provide resources
nodes.before: A pending order does not create available funds or unlimited credit.
nodes.after: The sending institution meets the applicable account and funding conditions.
nodes.explain: The bank must have the resources required by the service and account arrangements.
nodes.overlay: Available USDC and transaction resources are needed; reserves are not a holder’s spendable transaction account.

label: 4 · Service transfer
nodes.before: The covered order is awaiting its relevant service event.
nodes.after: The service processes payment under Regulation J and OC 6.
nodes.explain: The Fedwire event concerns the participating institutions. It is not by itself a customer-account receipt.
nodes.overlay: A token transfer is not a Fedwire settlement event. Bank-dollar settlement, if required, needs another leg.

label: 5 · Receiving bank
nodes.before: A receiving-bank event must be identified under the applicable rules.
nodes.after: Where the cited Article 4-A rule applies, acceptance generally creates the beneficiary bank’s duty to pay, subject to its conditions.
nodes.explain: Bank acceptance, its duty to pay and actual customer availability must be distinguished.
nodes.overlay: A receiving wallet balance can be USDC or an intermediary claim; it does not establish received bank dollars.

label: 6 · Recipient account
nodes.before: The recipient’s actual account treatment has not yet been reconciled.
nodes.after: The relevant credit and availability can be evidenced at the customer level.
nodes.explain: Obtain the beneficiary account record and apply its terms. Do not collapse it into the interbank receipt.
nodes.overlay: Direct Circle redemption is conditional on eligibility and a Circle Mint account.

label: Debt discharge
Separate legal test
nodes.before: A bank event exists, but its effect on the underlying debt must be assessed.
nodes.after: Applicable law and the original agreement determine the extent of discharge.
nodes.explain: This is a legal relationship, not a second movement of money. The cited New York example links originator payment to beneficiary-bank acceptance subject to conditions and exceptions.
nodes.overlay: USDC receipt is not automatically discharge of every dollar debt. Assess the accepted payment method.

label: 7 · Resolve exceptions
nodes.before: An error, return or dispute may require action after processing.
nodes.after: The responsible actor and remedy are identified under the governing transfer and account rules.
nodes.explain: Investigation is a branch when needed, not a step every successful payment must take.
nodes.overlay: Redemption, market sale and a dispute claim are different exits against different parties.

scenarios.title: Sending resources are insufficient
scenarios.before: The covered payment has not met the applicable funding condition.
scenarios.after: Identify the funding source or applicable processing response; do not mark the service transfer complete.
scenarios.explain: Hypothetical funding shortfall. Neither the message nor a token interface supplies unlimited credit.
scenarios.overlay: A token route still needs transferable assets and any required external funding.

scenarios.title: USDC received; direct redemption unavailable
scenarios.before: The recipient holds USDC but direct Circle redemption eligibility is not established.
scenarios.after: Identify a permitted issuer or intermediary exit and its terms before claiming bank-dollar payout.
scenarios.explain: Hypothetical comparison scenario under the cited USDC terms. Holding USDC and access to Circle Mint are different conditions. A market sale is not direct issuer redemption.
scenarios.overlay: No bank payout is established by the token balance. Identify the exact exit provider, timing, fees and receipt.

label: Hold transferable USDC
overlay_nodes.before: A prospective sender needs a transferable token holding.
overlay_nodes.after: The sender holds the relevant issuer-linked or intermediary claim.
overlay_nodes.explain: Acquisition can involve a separate issuer or intermediary route; it is not implied by a Fedwire instruction.
overlay_nodes.overlay: Identify exact asset, network, issuer and custody.

label: Transfer USDC
overlay_nodes.before: A holder authorizes a token transfer.
overlay_nodes.after: The recipient token holding changes under the supported token/network controls.
overlay_nodes.explain: This is an alternative-asset comparison, not part of the ordinary Fedwire sequence above.
overlay_nodes.overlay: Token transfer does not itself supply bank dollars.

label: Redeem / sell
overlay_nodes.before: The holder wants a different asset or bank-dollar exit.
overlay_nodes.after: An eligible issuer-redemption or intermediary sale route is required.
overlay_nodes.explain: Direct Circle redemption and exchange sale are different legal routes.

label: Bank payout evidence
overlay_nodes.before: Token transfer or redemption has not established bank receipt.
overlay_nodes.after: A matching bank-dollar receipt establishes that additional leg.
overlay_nodes.explain: This is an additional outcome to verify when bank dollars are requested, not a necessary event for someone choosing to keep USDC.
overlay_nodes.overlay: Identify the paying entity and actual recipient credit.

transaction_maps.scope: The three researched Steps & rights routes. Not every U.S. instrument, access model or exception has been mapped.
unmapped: Collateral pledges, margin calls and default waterfalls
Derivatives, FX and cross-border transaction routes

legal_routes_map.scope: U.S. research: all 26 function families now have at least one bounded route. This is coverage of the selected functions, not every legal alternative or eligible institution. Named profiles retain their source dates; current permissions, appointments and access must be established for the arrangement.
