routes.label: Issuer transfer agent · SEC registration
routes.trigger: The activity is an issuer transfer-agent function within the statutory registration perimeter.
routes.basis: Exchange Act §17A(c); appropriate-regulator registration
conditions: Confirm the covered security and statutory function.
For entities assigned to the SEC, establish effective registration.
Separately establish issuer appointment and the authoritative record.
routes.limit: A chain or technology vendor does not inherit its client’s transfer-agent registration.
eligible_categories: Transfer agents whose covered activities and entity category require registration with the SEC

routes.label: Bank transfer agent · OCC route
routes.trigger: The relevant entity falls within the national-bank category assigned to the OCC.
routes.basis: Transfer-agent registration with the appropriate banking regulator
conditions: Confirm exact entity category and applicable ARA.
Recover effective TA registration; a bank charter alone is insufficient.
Establish the issuer mandate and service scope.
routes.limit: No named bank is assessed under this route in this release.
eligible_categories: Bank transfer agents assigned to the OCC as appropriate regulatory agency

routes.label: Bank transfer agent · Federal Reserve route
routes.trigger: The entity falls within the state-member-bank, relevant subsidiary or bank-holding-company ARA category.
routes.basis: Transfer-agent registration through the Board
conditions: Verify statutory entity category.
Recover effective TA registration and restrictions.
Recover the issue-specific appointment.
routes.limit: An institution’s Federal Reserve relationship alone does not establish this role.
eligible_categories: Banking entities assigned to the Board as appropriate regulatory agency for transfer-agent functions

routes.label: Bank transfer agent · FDIC route
routes.trigger: The entity falls within the insured nonmember-bank or relevant subsidiary ARA category.
routes.basis: Transfer-agent registration through FDIC
conditions: Verify applicable entity category and registration.
Confirm issuer mandate and recordkeeping duties.
routes.limit: Deposit insurance does not itself grant a transfer-agent appointment.
eligible_categories: Banking entities assigned to FDIC as appropriate regulatory agency for transfer-agent functions

routes.label: Depository / clearing-agency entitlement records
routes.trigger: The record concerns intermediary securities entitlements and depository services rather than issuer registration.
routes.basis: Exchange Act clearing-agency framework plus DTC rules
conditions: Identify the exact service and participant tier.
Apply governing entitlement law and account rules.
Keep issuer and customer records distinct.
routes.limit: This route is not interchangeable with issuer-level transfer agency.
eligible_categories: Depository or clearing-agency entities acting within their permitted recordkeeping services

routes.label: SEC-registered clearing agency
routes.trigger: The entity performs securities clearing-agency functions.
routes.basis: Exchange Act §17A; registration and applicable clearing rules
conditions: Registration must cover the entity and function.
Identify CCP or depository service, asset and risk framework.
Membership and transaction acceptance remain additional gates.
routes.limit: DTC’s registration does not make it the CCP for every service; the function must be identified.
eligible_categories: Clearing agencies registered with the SEC for the relevant services

routes.label: Clearing-agency registration exemption
routes.trigger: The entity relies on relief rather than registration.
routes.basis: A specific applicable exemption/order
conditions: Recover exact relief, entity and activity.
Check products, conditions, effective period and ongoing obligations.
routes.limit: An exempt entity is not thereby SEC-registered. No entity-specific exemption is assessed here.
eligible_categories: Entities and activities covered by an applicable clearing-agency exemption

routes.label: Derivatives clearing organization
routes.trigger: The activity falls within the CEA derivatives-clearing function.
routes.basis: CEA §5b and applicable CFTC rules
conditions: Classify the contract and clearing activity.
Establish DCO registration or applicable relief and scope.
Review membership, margin and default terms.
routes.limit: Securities clearing and derivatives clearing are separate legal tests; named DCO permissions are not assessed here.
eligible_categories: Derivatives clearing organizations with the required registration or specific applicable relief

routes.label: Registered broker-dealer pathway
routes.trigger: The activity effects securities transactions in the relevant broker/dealer capacity.
routes.basis: Exchange Act definitions and §15(a)
conditions: Establish effective broker-dealer registration for the exact entity.
Check membership, business restrictions and customer/instrument scope.
Recover the distribution or transaction mandate.
routes.limit: Parent ownership or an API does not create broker-dealer authority.
eligible_categories: Registered broker-dealers acting within permitted business and membership conditions

routes.label: Broker-dealer operating under Regulation ATS
routes.trigger: The trading system uses the ATS route rather than exchange registration.
routes.basis: Regulation ATS and applicable broker-dealer requirements
conditions: Classify system functionality and instruments.
Recover appropriate ATS filings and broker-dealer status.
Apply subscriber, instrument and operating conditions.
routes.limit: An ATS filing is not Commission approval; operation and individual access need evidence.
eligible_categories: Broker-dealers operating an alternative trading system under the applicable Regulation ATS conditions

routes.label: National securities exchange registration
routes.trigger: The system performs exchange functions and uses the registered-exchange route.
routes.basis: Exchange Act §6 and applicable rules
conditions: Establish exchange registration and rulebook.
Identify membership, products and access requirements.
routes.limit: This is distinct from an ATS; no named exchange is assessed in this route view yet.
eligible_categories: Registered national securities exchanges

routes.label: DCM or SEF · derivatives-specific pathways
routes.trigger: The contract and execution function bring the venue within DCM or SEF requirements.
routes.basis: CEA designated-contract-market or swap-execution-facility framework
conditions: Choose the correct statutory pathway.
Recover the specific designation/registration and permissions.
Apply participant and product rules.
routes.limit: DCM and SEF are different tests; this is a research branch, not an entity authorization.
eligible_categories: Designated contract markets or registered swap execution facilities under their respective statutory routes

routes.label: New York virtual-currency license pathway
routes.trigger: The proposed function is covered New York virtual-currency business activity.
routes.basis: 23 NYCRR Part 200 and entity-specific approvals
conditions: Identify covered activity and territorial nexus.
Check license conditions and approved business scope.
Add product, custody or issuer-specific approvals where required.
routes.limit: Listed licensure is not proof that this selected function or product is authorized. Other laws remain relevant.
eligible_categories: Entities licensed for the relevant New York virtual-currency business activity

routes.label: New York limited-purpose trust charter · approved activity scope required
routes.trigger: The entity uses an applicable New York charter with permission for virtual-currency activity.
routes.basis: New York Banking Law route and superintendent approval
conditions: Identify exact chartered entity.
Recover approved virtual-currency business scope.
Confirm the selected product/function and required agreements.
routes.limit: A limited-purpose charter does not transfer to affiliates or establish every issuer/custody function.
eligible_categories: New York chartered trust companies with the separately approved activity scope

routes.label: Fund issuer · offering and subscription route
routes.trigger: The claim is a fund share, not a bank deposit or payment token.
routes.basis: Issuer documents plus applicable offering and fund law
conditions: Identify issuer and governing law.
Identify the offer’s jurisdictions and establish the applicable registration, exemption, or other offering route.
Apply investor eligibility, acceptance and funding conditions.
routes.limit: The agreement proves a named issuer, not the full current offering-law analysis.
eligible_categories: Identified fund issuers satisfying the relevant offering and organizational law

routes.label: Applicable custody regime + mandate
routes.trigger: The service safeguards specified assets for a client or fund.
routes.basis: Asset/client-specific custody law and contract
conditions: Select applicable regime before judging qualification.
Verify entity powers, eligible assets and possession/control arrangements.
Recover appointment, account title, segregation and subcustody terms.
routes.limit: Custody has several legal routes; a named appointment is not universal qualified-custodian status.
eligible_categories: Custodians eligible under the specific asset, client and regulatory custody regime

routes.label: Registered investment adviser pathway
routes.trigger: The activity is investment advice within the relevant statutory perimeter.
routes.basis: Advisers Act; federal/state registration allocation and exemptions
conditions: Identify advisory activity, client and jurisdiction.
Establish federal or state registration and any limits.
Recover current Form ADV and the advisory mandate.
routes.limit: The named affiliate is reported as registered in the later MD&A; current regulator verification and mandate remain separate.
eligible_categories: Investment advisers registered with the applicable federal or state authority

routes.label: Payment-system operating rules and access
routes.trigger: The role is operating the specified settlement system, not merely issuing a token.
routes.basis: CHIPS operating framework; participant and bank arrangements
conditions: Identify legal operator and exact service.
Recover applicable system, account and funding terms.
Separate operator, member and customer rights.
routes.limit: This system-specific route does not exhaust U.S. settlement services or grant another company account access.
eligible_categories: Legal system operators and admitted participants acting in their distinct system roles

routes.label: Express appointment and retained duties
routes.trigger: An issuer or system assigns specified servicing or correction powers.
routes.basis: Governing contract/rules plus applicable legal duties
conditions: Identify the principal and exact appointee.
Specify records, distributions, correction and liability scope.
Check that registration or other powers needed for the activity are separately satisfied.
routes.limit: A contract cannot confer statutory powers the appointee otherwise lacks.
eligible_categories: Appointed agents with the independent powers or registrations required for the delegated duties

routes.label: Proposed linked-record architecture
routes.trigger: Researching how the SEC’s proposed transfer-agent changes could affect records.
routes.basis: SEC Release 34-106246 · proposed
conditions: Track proposal versus final rule.
Do not use this branch as current permission.
routes.limit: No entity receives operative authority from this proposal.
eligible_categories: No current eligible category is created by this proposal

routes.label: Adviser exemption / reporting pathway
routes.trigger: The activity is investment advice within the relevant statutory perimeter.
routes.basis: Advisers Act; federal/state registration allocation and exemptions
conditions: Identify the exact applicable exemption.
Check its client, asset and activity limits.
Establish any reporting obligations and the mandate.
routes.limit: An exempt reporting adviser is not thereby a registered adviser. No currently assessed named player is attached to this branch.
eligible_categories: Advisers satisfying the precise exemption and any reporting conditions

routes.label: Specific broker/dealer exclusion or exception
routes.trigger: The activity effects securities transactions in the relevant broker/dealer capacity.
routes.basis: Exchange Act definitions and §15(a)
conditions: Identify the precise exclusion or exception and covered activity.
Check all entity, instrument and transaction conditions.
Do not infer relief merely from a technology or bank label.
routes.limit: No named entity has been assessed for this exception branch; do not treat it as registered status.
eligible_categories: Persons or activities meeting all conditions of a specific broker/dealer exclusion or exception

routes.label: Federal securities or derivatives-market authority
routes.trigger: A legally classified securities-market or derivatives-market activity calls for the applicable SEC or CFTC registration, designation, supervision, or rule route.
routes.basis: Federal securities laws and the Commodity Exchange Act, each within its statutory perimeter.
conditions: Classify the instrument, contract, and activity.
Identify the exact entity and applicable SEC, CFTC, or SRO route.
Recover current registration, designation, order, exemption, rulebook, and effective-date evidence.
eligible_categories: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
Commodity Futures Trading Commission
SEC or CFTC offices acting under delegated authority
Self-regulatory organizations only within their separate statutory rulemaking roles
routes.limit: Neither tokenization nor a technical ledger decides securities/commodity classification or creates SEC/CFTC permission.

routes.label: Federal bank chartering, supervision, and deposit-insurance route
routes.trigger: A U.S. banking activity requires a charter, supervision, deposit-insurance analysis, or a related federal banking permission.
routes.basis: Applicable National Bank Act, Federal Reserve, and Federal Deposit Insurance Act authorities.
conditions: Identify the exact legal entity and charter class.
Identify the applicable primary federal and state supervisor and any insurer.
Recover the current charter, approval, conditions, and product-specific authority.
eligible_categories: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation
Applicable state banking authority in its own statutory lane
routes.limit: Federal supervision, a bank affiliation, preliminary charter approval, or deposit insurance does not establish a particular product authority, bank account, or affiliate permission.

routes.label: Federal BSA/MSB registration plus bounded New York authorization route
routes.trigger: The proposed payment or value-transfer activity may fall within the federal MSB registration perimeter and/or covered New York virtual-currency activity.
routes.basis: 31 U.S.C. section 5330 and the FinCEN MSB registration framework; New York's separate virtual-currency authorization framework.
conditions: Classify the activity and territorial nexus.
Determine whether FinCEN MSB registration applies.
For New York activity, identify the exact license/charter, approved scope, conditions, and current status.
eligible_categories: Financial Crimes Enforcement Network for federal MSB registration
New York State Department of Financial Services for its New York virtual-currency authorization framework
routes.limit: Federal MSB registration is not a nationwide operating license; NYDFS evidence is a bounded New York route and does not resolve other states' requirements or securities, commodities, banking, sanctions, or consumer-protection law.

routes.label: Entity governing documents and formation-law route
routes.trigger: The question is who may direct a legal entity, appoint officers, authorize contracts, or allocate internal fiduciary and voting powers.
routes.basis: Applicable entity-formation law plus charter, bylaws/operating agreement, board or member action, and contract; Delaware corporate law is the bounded statutory example.
conditions: Identify the exact legal entity and formation jurisdiction.
Recover current governing documents and the relevant authorization record.
Separate entity governance from regulatory permission, network governance, and asset-holder rights.
eligible_categories: Boards of directors of corporations
Managers of manager-managed LLCs
Members of member-managed LLCs
Other entity governing bodies only as provided by applicable formation law and governing documents
routes.limit: A corporate board, foundation, DAO vote, or product committee does not obtain public-law authority or control a separately issued asset absent the governing instrument and applicable law.

routes.label: SRO rulebook governance subject to SEC process
routes.trigger: A securities SRO's participant, membership, trading, clearing, or disciplinary rule is the claimed source of governance.
routes.basis: Exchange Act section 19 proposed-rule process plus the SRO's effective rulebook.
conditions: Identify the SRO and exact rule version.
Confirm the rule's Commission filing/approval or effectiveness status as applicable.
Establish that the entity, participant, instrument, and event are within the rule's scope.
eligible_categories: National securities exchanges acting as SROs
Registered securities associations
Registered clearing agencies with applicable SRO rule obligations
routes.limit: An SRO's private operating rulebook is not a general federal statute, and a corporate or protocol rulebook is not an SRO rulebook merely because market participants use it.

routes.label: Title VIII designated-FMU public-authority and standards route
routes.trigger: The operator is an FSOC-designated financial market utility and the relevant statutory supervisory-agency framework applies.
routes.basis: Dodd-Frank Act Title VIII designation and supervisory framework.
conditions: Recover the specific FSOC designation and designated activity.
Identify the statutory supervisory agency and applicable risk-management standards.
Review the FMU's operative governance, recovery, and participant rules.
eligible_categories: Financial Stability Oversight Council
Statutory supervisory agencies for designated financial market utilities
Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System where the statute assigns the role
Securities and Exchange Commission where the statute assigns the role
Commodity Futures Trading Commission where the statute assigns the role
routes.limit: PFMI terminology, technical settlement capability, or market importance does not itself produce an FSOC designation or Title VIII governance obligation.

routes.label: FDIC insured-depository resolution route
routes.trigger: A failed insured depository institution enters the statutory FDIC resolution/receivership framework.
routes.basis: Federal Deposit Insurance Act and the applicable FDIC receivership authority.
conditions: Confirm the failed entity is the relevant insured depository institution.
Identify the receiver, deposits/accounts, assuming institution or payout path, and claim class.
Separate the bank from its parent, nonbank affiliates, custodial arrangements, and token issuer obligations.
eligible_categories: Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation acting as statutory receiver
FDIC-appointed receivers
Assuming depository institutions under the approved resolution transaction
routes.limit: FDIC insurance/resolution is not SIPC protection, does not insure investment losses or token value, and does not automatically cover a bank affiliate or a customer claim against a nonbank issuer.

routes.label: SIPA customer-property liquidation route
routes.trigger: A financially troubled SIPC-member broker-dealer has missing customer cash or securities and a SIPA liquidation is applicable.
routes.basis: Securities Investor Protection Act and the liquidation case.
conditions: Confirm SIPC-member broker-dealer status and the statutory trigger.
Establish customer status, asset classification, account facts, and claim deadlines.
Apply SIPA's limits and the trustee/court process.
eligible_categories: Securities Investor Protection Corporation
Court-appointed SIPA trustees
SIPA liquidation estates
routes.limit: SIPC is distinct from FDIC deposit insurance; it does not protect market-value loss, ordinary investment losses, commodities/FX claims, or digital/crypto assets outside SIPA's security definition.

routes.label: Federal bankruptcy court and estate-administration route
routes.trigger: An eligible debtor's insolvency is governed by the Bankruptcy Code rather than a specialized bank, broker-dealer, insurer, or other resolution regime.
routes.basis: Bankruptcy Code eligibility and the applicable chapter/court process.
conditions: Identify the exact debtor legal entity and its eligibility.
Identify the chapter, venue, court orders, estate fiduciary, and property/claim characterization.
Test whether a specialized insolvency, receivership, or resolution statute applies instead.
eligible_categories: United States bankruptcy courts
U.S. Trustee Program
Court-appointed case trustees
Debtors in possession where the Bankruptcy Code permits
routes.limit: Bankruptcy is not a catch-all: domestic banks are excluded by section 109, and specialized regimes can govern other regulated entities. A token ledger does not by itself identify estate property, perfection, custody, or priority.

routes.label: Covered clearing-agency recovery and wind-down planning route
routes.trigger: A covered SEC-registered clearing agency is within Rule 17Ad-22's applicable recovery and orderly-wind-down requirements.
routes.basis: Exchange Act clearing-agency framework and SEC Rule 17Ad-22.
conditions: Identify the registered clearing agency and whether it is covered by the cited provisions.
Recover the current recovery/wind-down plan, default rules, liquidity arrangements, and participant obligations.
Apply the exact service, product, member, and event rather than an organization-wide label.
eligible_categories: Covered SEC-registered clearing agencies
Default-management and recovery-plan actors named by an effective clearing-agency rulebook
routes.limit: A recovery plan is not an observed resolution outcome, a customer guarantee, or a universal default waterfall for broker-dealers, banks, custodians, issuers, or blockchain networks.

routes.label: Direct registered holder of a security
routes.trigger: An investor elects direct registration for a security whose issuer offers it.
routes.basis: SEC describes direct registration as the investor's name appearing on the issuer's books, maintained by the issuer or its transfer agent.
eligible_categories: natural person
legal entity
conditions: Issuer offers direct registration.
Investor meets issuer/transfer-agent onboarding and account requirements.
For a DRS transfer, the security and transfer agent are DTC DRS eligible.
routes.limit: This is a direct-registration route; it does not establish that every issuer offers it, that a token ledger is the issuer record, or that the issuer is itself the holder.

routes.label: Beneficial holder through a street-name intermediary
routes.trigger: A customer holds securities through a broker-dealer or bank in street name.
routes.basis: SEC describes the intermediary as recorded on issuer books and the intermediary as maintaining the record identifying the customer as beneficial owner.
eligible_categories: natural person
legal entity
account customer of an intermediary
conditions: Intermediary accepts the customer and account under its applicable program terms and legal requirements.
Security is available through that intermediary's custody/nominee arrangement.
routes.limit: Beneficial interest is distinct from appearing as registered owner on issuer books. This does not make an issuer, token administrator, or transfer agent the beneficial holder.

routes.label: BUIDL subscription/access gate
routes.trigger: A prospective investor seeks to acquire an interest in the named fund product.
routes.basis: The March 14, 2024 filed BUIDL agreement allocates subscription, issuer and registration functions; the current offering and subscription documents remain controlling.
eligible_categories: The issuer or authorized appointee empowered to accept subscriptions under the fund documents
conditions: Apply the operative offering, subscription, eligibility, sanctions/AML, and transfer documents for the relevant share class and jurisdiction.
Identify whether the result is direct registration, intermediary-held beneficial interest, or another contractual record arrangement.
routes.limit: The named fund is the issuer controlling the subscription arrangement, not the investor. Current eligibility terms and acceptance authority still require the operative offering documents.

routes.label: DFS-supervised stablecoin holder redemption gate
routes.trigger: A lawful holder requests direct redemption from a DFS-supervised issuer.
routes.basis: NYDFS requires a covered issuer policy to confer a timely par-redemption right on a lawful holder, subject to reasonable conditions including successful onboarding.
eligible_categories: DFS-supervised issuers and authorized onboarding agents applying the covered product redemption policy
conditions: The particular coin is issued under DFS supervision and applicable issuer policy applies.
Holder/designee successfully onboards and meets compliant-order conditions.
Issuer has required DFS approval and current product terms.
routes.limit: Circle is issuer-context only, never the holder. Guidance does not prove that a particular Circle holder has direct redemption rights under current terms.

routes.label: Covered stablecoin issuer reserve policy
routes.trigger: A DFS-supervised issuer maintains backing assets; where Circle Reserve Fund is used, its disclosed manager manages fund investments and operations.
routes.basis: NYDFS stablecoin guidance sets backing, custody, segregation and liquidity conditions for covered issuers.
eligible_categories: DFS-supervised stablecoin issuers subject to the guidance, acting through properly appointed reserve providers
conditions: Identify the covered issuer and approved product.
Establish the reserve policy, permitted assets, segregation, custody and reporting arrangements.
Separate issuer policy responsibility from the fund manager and custodian appointments.
routes.limit: This covered-issuer policy route does not itself appoint an investment manager or prove any entity’s current product approval.

routes.label: National-bank fiduciary/trustee route
routes.trigger: A national bank seeks to act as trustee or other fiduciary for a particular instrument or estate.
routes.basis: 12 USC 92a and implementing 12 CFR Part 9 distinguish fiduciary powers from the governing instrument and account duties.
eligible_categories: National banks with applicable OCC fiduciary authority, validly appointed to the particular fiduciary account
conditions: Establish applicable fiduciary permission and any exceptions under Part 9.
Recover the instrument or court order appointing the bank and defining duties.
Apply fiduciary asset, recordkeeping and administration controls.
routes.limit: Charter, custody service, or listing does not establish trustee appointment. This does not determine state-chartered trust company or Delaware-law mechanics.

routes.label: FICC/GSD direct netting participation
routes.trigger: A firm seeks direct FICC/GSD netting and settlement as Netting Member.
routes.basis: DTCC describes Full Netting Membership as direct GSD participation and names banks, broker-dealers, inter-dealer brokers, FCMs, clearing agencies and investment companies as eligible categories; GSD Rules govern qualification/obligations.
eligible_categories: bank
broker-dealer
inter-dealer broker
futures commission merchant
clearing agency
investment company
conditions: FICC accepts application under current GSD Rules and membership standards.
Applicant meets operative legal, financial, operational, and settlement requirements.
routes.limit: Listed category is not automatic admission. Direct participation is separate from sponsored, agent-clearing, and executing-firm access.

routes.label: FICC/GSD sponsored participation
routes.trigger: A qualified legal entity seeks GSD access through a Sponsoring Member rather than direct netting membership.
routes.basis: Rule 3A permits a relationship between approved Sponsoring Member and person accepted by FICC as its Sponsored Member. DTCC states the entry conditions as approved-jurisdiction legal entity plus an available sponsor.
eligible_categories: legal entity in FICC-approved jurisdiction
eligible GSD Netting Member applying as Sponsoring Member
conditions: Sponsoring applicant meets Rule 3A/current standards and is approved.
FICC accepts entity as that sponsor's Sponsored Member.
Parties comply with current rules, guaranty, and service documents.
routes.limit: Sponsored access is separate from direct Netting Membership; a service page does not replace GSD Rules.

routes.label: Appointed investment manager of a reserve fund
routes.trigger: Reserve exposure is held through a fund whose investment manager exercises the investment mandate.
routes.basis: The fund’s governing and advisory documents allocate discretion; the applicable adviser and fund requirements apply independently.
eligible_categories: Investment managers with the applicable regulatory status and an effective fund mandate
conditions: Identify the exact fund and investment-manager legal entity.
Recover the current advisory mandate, investment limits and board oversight.
Keep the fund’s asset custody and issuer’s redemption obligations separate.
routes.limit: The filing supports a named Circle Reserve Fund arrangement, not blanket powers for the BlackRock parent or every reserve asset.

routes.label: FICC membership decision under GSD rules
routes.trigger: An applicant seeks GSD membership or a sponsored relationship.
routes.basis: GSD Rules 2, 2A and 3A allocate admission and continuing requirements.
eligible_categories: FICC acting through its authorized membership decision process
conditions: Identify the requested membership class and applicable rule.
Obtain the required acceptance and satisfy continuing conditions.
routes.limit: FICC’s decision role does not make its parent, a technology vendor or a sponsor the final membership authority.

routes.label: Fedwire participant payment or securities-transfer instruction
routes.trigger: A Fedwire participant sends a Funds payment order or Securities transfer message under the applicable service’s legal framework.
routes.basis: Fedwire Funds: Regulation J and OC 6. Fedwire Securities: applicable book-entry securities regulations and OC 7.
conditions: Identify the eligible participant, its Reserve Bank account or securities account, and the exact Fedwire service.
Apply the service's authorization/security procedure, message format, account, asset, and cutoff conditions.
For securities, establish Fedwire eligibility and any transfer-against-payment conditions; for funds, establish a payment order accepted under the applicable procedure.
eligible_categories: Fedwire Funds participant or authorized sender under its service arrangement
Fedwire Securities participant
authorized service provider acting through the participant's applicable Fedwire arrangement
routes.limit: This is a Fedwire-specific authorization route. A wallet signature, API call, or message on another system does not inherit Fedwire authority or establish legal effect for a different claim.

routes.label: FedLine electronic-access and designated service-provider route
routes.trigger: A Reserve Bank institution or authorized service provider accesses an identified Reserve Bank electronic service through the applicable OC 5 and service terms.
routes.basis: Operating Circular 5 and the relevant Fedwire service terms; the Fedwire form route expressly contemplates designation of a third-party service provider.
conditions: Identify the institution, electronic connection, access credentials, and exact Reserve Bank service.
Recover the applicable OC 5/service terms and any third-party service arrangement or API terms.
Establish separately the participant that has authority to originate the payment or securities instruction and the service-specific acceptance/finality event.
eligible_categories: Reserve Bank service participant
FedLine subscriber
Reserve Bank-authorized API service provider
designated Fedwire third-party service provider
routes.limit: This is an authorized Reserve Bank electronic-access route, not a general interoperability license. Electronic transport does not make the provider the account holder, sender, securities participant, title authority, or settlement obligor.

routes.label: Registered transfer agent using DLT in its official record
routes.trigger: A registered transfer agent uses DLT for all or part of its official master securityholder file for a covered security.
routes.basis: SEC staff DLT FAQ Q10–Q11, Exchange Act transfer-agent framework, and the transfer agent's existing applicable recordkeeping and safeguarding duties.
conditions: Identify the registered transfer agent, covered security, issuer appointment, and official master securityholder file.
Establish how the on-chain and off-chain components together remain secure, accurate, current, producible, and retained as required.
Recover the applicable correction, reconciliation, fork, access, and vendor-control procedures.
eligible_categories: SEC-registered transfer agent
bank transfer agent registered with the appropriate federal banking regulator
routes.limit: The FAQ does not provide a standalone legal-effect route for a generic network operator, validator, sequencer, bridge, or protocol-governance group. Their legal effect remains a separate arrangement-specific question.

routes.label: Technology vendor or outsourced infrastructure under accountable-client controls
routes.trigger: A regulated or contractually accountable firm uses a vendor, linked ledger, database, wallet system, or infrastructure provider to perform part of its operating model.
routes.basis: Service contract plus the accountable client's applicable statutory and regulatory obligations. For supervised banking organizations, SR 23-4 gives risk-management guidance for third-party relationships and explicitly creates no new requirements.
conditions: Identify the client that retains the regulated or contractual duty.
Recover the vendor agreement, data/control access, security, continuity, audit, incident, correction, and exit provisions.
Test the vendor's own activity separately if it also performs a regulated function.
eligible_categories: software vendor
cloud or infrastructure provider
ledger/database provider
wallet or key-management vendor
systems integrator
recordkeeping transfer agent using linked technical systems
routes.limit: Vendor participation does not relocate a regulated client's recordkeeping, reporting, safeguarding, or examination duties, and it does not prove the vendor holds an independent regulatory permission. SR 23-4 is guidance, not a new vendor authorization rule.

routes.label: CFTC swap reporting counterparty or registered-entity route
routes.trigger: The transaction is a CFTC-regulated swap and Part 45 assigns a reporting counterparty or reporting task to a SEF, DCM, or DCO.
routes.basis: CEA swap-data framework and 17 CFR Parts 45 and 49.
conditions: Classify the instrument as a CFTC-regulated swap and identify the reporting hierarchy or registered-entity rule.
Select an appropriate SDR and meet its data, validation, timing, and access requirements.
A counterparty may contract with a facilitator to submit data, but preserve the assigned reporting party's responsibility and evidence of successful acceptance.
eligible_categories: swap dealer
major swap participant
other reporting counterparty as allocated by Part 45
swap execution facility
designated contract market
derivatives clearing organization
third-party reporting facilitator acting for the responsible reporter
routes.limit: A delegate submits or facilitates only under the responsible party's arrangement; it is neither automatically the reporting counterparty nor an SDR. A generic blockchain log or oracle feed is not an SDR report.

routes.label: CFTC swap data repository acceptance route
routes.trigger: A CFTC-regulated swap report must be accepted, maintained, and made available within the statutory SDR framework.
routes.basis: CEA section 21 and 17 CFR Part 49; entity-specific CFTC repository status and service terms.
conditions: Confirm the exact legal entity, CFTC status, asset-class scope, and current rules.
Establish participant eligibility, repository selection, technical access, and successful data validation/acceptance.
Keep repository maintenance separate from the counterparty or registered entity's reporting duty and correction duty.
eligible_categories: CFTC-registered or provisionally registered swap data repository within its approved scope
routes.limit: Repository listing is not proof that a particular transaction is reportable, accepted, correctly reported, or within a named repository's service scope.

routes.label: SEC security-based swap reporting and registered SDR route
routes.trigger: The instrument is a security-based swap subject to Regulation SBSR, rather than a CFTC swap or an ordinary tokenized security record.
routes.basis: Exchange Act section 13(n), Regulation SBSR, and the SEC security-based-swap data-repository framework.
conditions: Classify the instrument and responsible reporting person under the SEC regime.
Confirm the registered SDR, asset class, reporting format, participant agreement, and compliance date applicable to the transaction.
Do not merge the CFTC and SEC repository routes merely because service providers have related names.
eligible_categories: security-based swap dealer
major security-based swap participant
counterparty or platform assigned a reporting duty under Regulation SBSR
SEC-registered security-based swap data repository
routes.limit: This route does not govern ordinary securities-token recordkeeping, a transfer agent's master securityholder file, or CFTC-regulated swaps.

routes.label: FICC sponsoring member · sponsor side
routes.trigger: A qualifying Netting Member seeks approval to sponsor eligible Sponsored Members.
routes.basis: FICC GSD Rule 3A and applicable service terms
eligible_categories: Eligible Netting Members approved by FICC as Sponsoring Members
conditions: Establish the exact legal entity and qualifying membership.
Confirm FICC sponsorship approval and the particular service.
Identify the sponsored member, agreements, guarantee and applicable obligations.
routes.limit: Sponsor approval does not identify every sponsored customer or establish admission for a particular transaction.

routes.label: Fund shareholder · holding form must be established
routes.trigger: An entity owns fund shares of record or beneficially.
routes.basis: Fund governing documents and ownership records
eligible_categories: Eligible fund shareholders under the offering and account terms
conditions: Confirm investor eligibility and subscription acceptance.
Establish whether ownership is registered or beneficial and identify the recordkeeper/intermediary.
Verify the holding date, share class and applicable rights.
routes.limit: A disclosure saying record or beneficial ownership does not resolve which holding form applies.

routes.label: DTC nominee registered-holder route
routes.trigger: A security is deposited with DTC and the issuer or its transfer agent maintains the shareholder list showing DTC's nominee.
routes.basis: SEC staff guidance states that Cede & Co. appears as sole registered owner on the shareholder list for securities deposited with DTC by DTC participants.
eligible_categories: DTC nominee for securities deposited with DTC
conditions: Identify the particular security and confirm that it is deposited with DTC.
Recover the applicable issuer or transfer-agent shareholder list or equivalent record.
Keep the DTC nominee position separate from DTC participants and their customers' beneficial interests.
routes.limit: This route establishes a registered nominee category only. It does not establish ownership by a participant or customer, securities entitlement, voting authority, or a particular token ledger's legal effect.
